Divide by Sheep is one of the most fun math puzzle games I have played ever since I joined Steam nearly three years ago.
The main objective of putting varying amounts of sheep onto the live-saving rafts (and later on even wolves and pigs, all with their own quirks when moving them from island to island) is not as simple as it seems at first. Sure, the start into the game is very commonly done. Easy puzzle first, some jumping about, almost no way of mucking it up.
Then come the fences.
And the laser barriers.
The wolves eating the sheep.
Pigs making everything slippery.
Islands of varying size not permitting for more than a certain amount of animals to pass.
Islands getting blown up when they are left.
Tiles that set sheep on fire.
And even a big, big, stomping idol that squishes anything in its way.
It's hilarious, and it's a fun brain-tease. Let's just hope that Death doesn't make the mistake again to flood the Earth in order to have more friends.
Fantastic, good learning curve, cute art style and music, and well worth the price.

Edna & Harvey: Harvey's New Eyes is a darkly whimsical point n' click adventure reminiscent of classic dark humor titles like Maniac Mansion or Sam & Max. If you don't enjoy twisted humor then this game is probably not for you. However, if you think you could find hilarity in the untimely deaths of several nasty orphan children, then I definitely recommend this game for you! Overall it's a solid game with a funny storyline that will occasionally make you feel guilty for chuckling and good puzzles that won't have you scratching your head for too long. That said, the animation and art style is a bit garish and jerky - very different from most other Daedalic titles. It's a style that seems to complement the story, in which the main character is a little girl who is probably schizophrenic, so it didn't bother me. But if you need your games to be pretty and fluid, again, you might be disappointed here. I had a lot of fun playing it and would probably play it through again.

Harvey's New Eyes was a casual (almost hesitant) purchase. However, it proved to be a pleasant surprise.
The narration at first draws you into a storybook tale about the protagonist, Lilli, and sets the mood for what seems to be a rather childish and cliché story. As you continue, the dialog and narration slowly become darker, yet the game never loses its humourous touch. It's entertaining and engaging in the most unexpected way possible. The dark humour, in my opinion, is what sets this point-and-click apart from others.
On occasion, the game has potential for glitching (for example, my inventory items would sometimes appear to be 'floating' when I opened the tab), and the game starts out slow and pleasant at first, but the story progresses almost a little too quickly for my taste toward the end.
Overall, though, I'd recommend this to any point-and-click fanatic who's looking for something a little different. The mature/immature atmospheric blend may be bewildering at first, but in the end, it's entertainment that's well worth your time.

I first bought this game in 2005 (back when CD-Roms were still a thing), and have been playing this game on and off ever since. I could talk about the bugs (there are plenty), the glitches (try beating the game without I patch, I dare you) or anything like that, but honestly, it is not relevant at all when it comes to this game, not in 2017 at least.
This old, little game that many have never even had the pleasure to hear about, is still supported by a loyal community that have made this game something very special. They adopted a game that was left in a very unfinished state and not only fixed what was broken, but recovered and completed unfinished and unused portions of the game as well as add new content to create a one-of-a-kind game that anyone who loves RPGs, Vampires, Role-playing or just a good game in general will enjoy.
The game itself, even before it was patched, is unique and charming. You play as a vampire in a gritty, dark version of Los Angeles. You are given nearly complete freedom as to how you want to play. You can talk your way out any situation, use violence to get the job done, or sneak around and avoid dealing with people altogether. There's 7 "clans" to play as, and each one offers a unique experience which is better suited for one style of gameplay or the other (good luck charming your way through the game as a Nosferatu).
The characters you meet are memorable, and your dialogue choices really have an impact on how they interact with you. In some cases their lives may even depend on your choices. You'll find yourself hating, liking or at the very least caring about some of these characters, and will remember them long after you beat the game. The locations are likewise interesting, memorable and unique. From the dangerous streets of Downtown L.A. to dark Griffith Park and from the sewers under Hollywood to a haunted mansion in Santa Monica, you will not be bored with your surroundings (even if the graphics are dated).
I could go on and on, but you should really see for yourself. Make sure you patch the game, and then immerse yourself in a World of Darkness. You will not be dissappointed and be drawn to this game time and time again.

Really, I don't see the need even to review: the game speaks for itself even all these years later. As I write this VTMB is 13 years old and yet it has stood the test of time as being one of the greatest games ever, the sort of a game whose mere mention on a forum can convince *someone* to reinstall it. It's a damn shame Troika went under, CCP cancelled the MMO, and that it was overshadowed by HL2 as they both used the same engine and wanted Half Life out earlier (frankly idgaf about GabeN releasing HL3 or not but if only a new World of Darkness game...) But, then again, Vampire the Masquerade: Bloodlines could just be fated to be one of those games where no studio is ever going to own up to the original. To me, it is like the StarCraft of modern RPGs, where no matter how hard they try all the new material would just be crappy DLCs and an underwhelming experience lacking the true love that went into the first.
The good:
Painstakingly recreated the original gothic-punk noir atmosphere with the right balance of humor and in-jokes (much akin to the original Fallout games and why Fallout 3 is ridiculed by old fans) and perfect atmosphere. For anyone who's ever been a fan of what White Wolf made with PnP and their novels/source materials, this is great, and serves as an excellent primer and introduction for those that haven't.
The soundtrack is awesome. Also very well done for helping set the tone of the whole game.
Mood in general is very grimdark in the tragic sense--you get less the feel of "whoa superpowers" and more the grinding tragedy where existentialism may well be the less angsty and horrid option than the ancient being(s) being very plausibly real, with you as ultimately a set piece no matter how bad you think you are (often literally).
The storytelling and character interactions. Just superb writing.
Replayability: almost every single person to play this game has gone through at least twice, three times being the average. The replay value is possibly the best I've ever seen for a game that actually follows a semi-linear story. Different clans, dialogue options, and playstyles, with the option of multiple endings means you're likely to only see at most 2/3 of the game on your first play through no matter what you do--and that's just the storyline(s). In terms of disciplines (abilities and spells) and various playstyles, one playthrough is probably 1/4 the content. Make sure Malkavians are one of your runs.
The Bad:
Certain stats are all but useless and things don't translate as well from the PnP. Most common example is loss of humanity, which doesn't affect a whole lot in the game and is fairly easy to replenish which is not like the original content at all. Still, what is lost in translation is probably unnoticeable to anyone not familiar with the setting. The only noticeable parts are things like Seduction which is an almost entirely useless stat.
The combat system. It's not actually as horrible as I thought at first especially compared to KoTOR, but it's still pretty bad, although use of firearms is decent enough and for its time isn't really that bad. Besides, if you're looking for a hack and slash this game isn't for you. The main reason is due to
Bugs. The game wasn't polished at release so needs a patch. My very first run through had a Kuei Jin stuck in mid air as I slashed him helplessly. Most bugs have been fixed otherwise.
Lastly it has had a fairly dedicated community including people from the actual project still working on it after release just out of dedication and love for the game, which in its own right should tell you something.

One Way Heroics is simple: pick your class, stats, and perks, and start heading to the right to flee the advancing darkness. The game is perfect for play in short bursts, and can often be found very cheap in the midst of a sale, so you may as well pick it up!

Trials Evolution on the Xbox 360 is my favorite video game of all time. I am ranked around 6000th on the overall leaderboard, and have devoted over 4 days of my time to getting platinum on every track in the game.
This PC port, however, is severely lacking. If you haven't used it before, the UPlay interface is atrocious, and its pitiful that Ubisoft requires their 3rd party software for all their games. The menu navigation is clearly designed for controllers, as sometimes you click things, but other times you are required to use the arrow keys (not WASD, arrow keys only) to navigate the menus and then hit enter to select. To be frank, if you are not playing with a controller with analog triggers, you are not playing the game correctly, but for those who don't have them they should be able to navigate menus effectively with a mouse.
Do NOT buy this game if you do not meet the RECOMMENDED requirements (if you have any doubts, give the demo a try). As a 360 port, this game was built to run on certain hardware, and if you don't have the hardware, it will perform VERY poorly. For some reason, the game engine is tied to a 60 fps framerate, and if you dip below that (believe me, if you don't meet the recommended requirements you will not reach 60 fps) the game suffers from severe stuttering, rendering it unplayable for some. With limited graphical settings to mess with, this isn't a problem you can fix, and it doesn't seem to be a problem Ubisoft or RedLynx is willing to address.
If you meet the recommended requirements, you should absolutely buy this game. It is a perfect blend of developed gameplay with great arcadey elements with great online leaderboard integration. The multiplayer has some problems, but the mere fact that they let you play user-generated tracks with your friends makes up for it as far as I am concerned. A robust track creator will keep the hardcore fans content for years to come. Its a shame that this version is bogged down by poor controls, UPlay, and a general laziness in porting the game engine.

TL;DR: A very well designed RPG, both in story and gameplay. Rough in both as well, not easy to finish and not just because of combat.
LISA is a definitely unique RPG experience. Set in a world that is reminiscent of Children of Men, albeit with a far more Fallout with rednecks aesthetic to it. While some parts of the game feel a bit immature (buttcracks and pixel man-nipples abound), the story itself is amazingly well done and told, with themes of abuse, addiction, failure, and the like. It is hard to talk about the story more than that without spoiling things, so it is best to play it yourself, and multiple times. The game is very good at showing and implying without outright telling. A lot of things are only talked about in a roundabout way, which makes the game feel all the more interesting.
Combat wise, it is a JRPG, in that all combat takes place on a different screen, where you have to whittle down HP. That said, the game is great about having practically every encounter be a unique enemy with their own sprite, and typically not random. Enemies jump out at you from behind walls, sometimes even avoidable to make the fight easier (they miss you, trip and fall, and act very different while faceplanted). The game has loads of characters, and the design is admirable in that all of them are pretty unique. Not to say all of them are useful in the endgame, there are definately winners, but you can tell that each character has a design concept in mind, and they are all truly unique. Some characters use the 'dial' system where you use directionals to input commands, potentially using combos (though often its easier to just use the combos from the skill menu with a slight hit to damage), while others use more standard skills, others use TP which is increased by receiving/dealing damage. A lot of import is balancing characters so they support each other, especially with status effects. One of the best characters in the game is great not because of damage he deals, but because he can cause oil/blind, which amplifies other character's fire damage. There are only a few areas to 'grind' in the game, increasing the difficulty a bit, but the game doesn't need a very high level to finish.
Most of the difficulty, sans optional bosses and a few endgame enemies, is from the choices you have to make. The game is absolutely brutal in forcing tough choices on you. Give up characters, or permanently cripple your main character. Take a drug that prevents you from getting an ending and severely boost stats...or deal with crippling addiction on several characters. At one point the game even forces you to use your characters in Russian roulette in order to proceed, with no warning. Later on you can go back to play it more to earn a lot more money and a character afterwards. While all of these are likely something that will cause some save-scumming, they are not entirely avoidable, and in order to get the true ending you need to play on PAIN mode, which makes every save point one use only. Later game combat enemies will also occasionally have perma-death moves, further amplifying the need for a large roster of characters.
In short, the game is a truly unique and enjoyable experience, if difficult to play due to the rough nature of the story and choices. The game is not that long, about 10 or so hours give or take optional things, though if you want to 100% the game it requires at least three playthroughs. More than worth the price of entry.

Very good game. There's a lot of challenging stuff to wrap your head around.
I would honestly recommend getting LISA: The Joyful as well, as that actually finishes the story - one complaint I could have about the first game is that while you do feel somewhat sympathetic towards Brad, a lot of things really don't make sense until The Joyful is completed - particularly Buddy's actions. I understand that's part of the storyteller's license, but I feel like they should have actually been one game ( perhaps seperated into ACT I and ACT II ).
I could see why the decision was made to keep them seperate ( because Buddy and Brad play very differently ), but you miss out on the whole story until you finish Joyful, and that's the main draw to this game - the narrative. LISA: The Painful does end on a good stopping point, however.
The gameplay is pretty decent. The static menu-based system ends up being OK because of all the outrageous characters, and Brad's combo system ( and others ) is pretty fun. It's got a lot of secrets and hidden gems , so people who loved playing old 16 bit JRPGS with tons of secrets will enjoy that aspect of LISA. Other than that though, its a pretty standard RPG. It tends to be a little more on the difficult side because resources are scarce ( and you can't really "grind" very well ), but is overall a fairly quick playthrough unless you activate Pain Mode.
A generic complaint I could make against BOTH games is that there are times when it is not clear - at all - what a dialogue choice will do. In particular there is a ( actually CLARIFIED but still unclear ) dialogue option with Terry the Hint Lord, and chosing "Pain Mode" ends up changing the game to a point where I almost stopped playing. Effectively, in Pain Mode, all the monsters are harder, and you can only use each save point ONCE.
That's a huge change to suggest in dialogue, or even to just wash away as being "Hard Mode", and while I can appreciate Ding's passion for forcing us to make choices with unclear results, there are a couple of places where this is just taken too far and will deter people who would otherwise enjoy the game from doing so.
That said, I would recommend this game to anyone who wanted a "new" RPG experience.

I personally enjoyed The Few quite a lot, despite a few shortcomings the game has.
Most complaints people have about the game is that its scope is somewhat limited: you command the RAF during the Battle of Britain and that means your main aim is to coordinate air defence. A lot of people would love to play as the Luftwaffe or to add later war RAF air raids against France and Germany, but quite frankly that doesn't take away from the game itself - it's more of a 'we would like this to continue!'.
Another thing often heard is its lack of realism in many regards and that's obviously true. The optics are fairly clear but all done in a cartoon style, which I personally found charming, but that's down to taste. Also the mechanics aren't overly realistic - obviously the top-down 2D playing field imposes certain limits here, but on the other side also makes sure the game stays accessible and easy to enjoy for everyone.
The AI in the game is a bit of a mixed bag, really. Of course it does have certain limitations eventually and once you play a longer campaign those become very apparent, like there are some tricks for which the Luftwaffe pilots always seem to fall, but quite frankly the same (and sometimes worse) holds true for many AAA titles. On the other hand I very much liked how the different levels of experience showed in the pilot AI: while rookies go straight for their targets, the more experienced flyers will engage in more advanced maneouvres on their own initiative, making use of blind spots and plane advantages.
Another thing actually done well and worth mentioning is the voice acting, which comes in different languages depending on squadron (the Polish developers obviously made a point of not forgetting that plenty of foreign squadrons took part in the battle - I didn't find that annoying at all, but some early-version reviews claimed that to be overdone) and, while eventually limited, does a good job of being informative, immersive and still not breaking the cartoony feel of the game.
So, in conclusion this is not a simulation, it's a strategy game more on the casual side. It's not perfect by all means, but it does a lot of things right and as none of the popular complaints really get in the way of enjoying the game, I don't see any reason not to recommend it to almost anybody.

Thanks to its decent presentation, “The Few” looks at first like a beer and pretzels sort of strategy game... excepting you’d better bring a dozen beers and several pounds of snacks, because the pace is excruciating. Basically what could have been the light tactical part of the game boils down to a mindless clicker, as there is next to nothing you can influence or need to figure out. You are just asked to keep paying attention, because otherwise, Britannia will fall, supposedly.
Indeed, shan’t you intercept the bombers, you will experience their deadly German accuracy.
The game annoyingly lacks attention to minor details, making the experience aggravating, especially in regard to drawing flight plans, or just the main time-acceleration mechanic.
Now that I type this, and I think about the layout of the game, I am noticing that, under its WW2 coat, “The Few” unveils forms akin to those of an extremely barebone tower-defence game. That was not my thing.

It's a fun little game. You spend half your time building radar installations, training new pilots, setting up patrol routes and so on. The other half of your time will be spent commanding your fighters in the air to air missions.
Defending the British iles is pretty straightforward, you set your planes up to fly a little patrol flight around their airfield, build some new airfields, buy some more planes, and that's it really. There's not much to it and that's a bit of a shame, but it's fun enough.
The air combat is just as simplistic as the command mode, you draw paths for individual planes to follow and attempt to shoot down the enemy. There's only 10-or-so plane types in total of which you can command only 2. And while that's pretty realistic I would've enjoyed hunting submarines with floatplanes as a side gig.
All in all, 2 bucks was a steal for this bundle of fun, and the developer is free to cash in another fiver whenever they make a sequal with more stuff to do.

HSL is a very old-school roguelike with the usual turn-based movement and permadeath, but does have decent pixel graphics and can be completely mouse-driven.  The difficulty is just as brutal and unforgiving as the ancient and free ascii/tileset roguelikes.  The only mercy is that stronger playable characters are unlocked through number of deaths as well as wins so, since you will be dying a lot, it won't all be in vain.
You start with a warrior, archer and wizard and, from there, can unlock around 30 additional classes to play.  There are a handful of different quests you can undertake, which will decide the types of enemies you'll be up against, dungeon layout and general mood.
Besides having achievements, there is nothing special or fun about Hack, Slash, Loot in comparison to all the free roguelikes out there.  I would only recommend paying for it to a hardcore roguelike enthusiast; anyone else who wants a traditional roguelike on Steam should just play Dungeons of Dredmor, Sword of the Stars: The Pit or Tales of Maj'Eyal.

In the 1930s, Alphonse Gabriel "Al" Capone was at his strongest, running the market of Chicago and much of the United States when it came to illegal alcohol. He was brutal, efficient, deadly, and most of all, he never left a wrong doing go unpunished. He is to this day, arguably the most famous outlaw in the history of the United States.
In Mafia II, you are not exactly Al Capone, but you are certainly a force to be reckoned with.
Mafia II(By 2K Czech) is not a good 'mobster game' for those people who want a 'start from the dirtheap, rise to the stars' sort of game, where you start out a simple footsoldier and rise to be the Kingpin of crime themself. In Mafia II, you play as an ex- US Soldier, and upstarting Mobster, named Vito Scarletta. He comes back from the war, and gets included into the Mob world right from the start by his childhood friend, Joe, who uses Mob connections to do so.
Vito goes on to being a key element in a story ripe with loyalty, betrayal, murder, and desperation. Only his training with weapons, and his ability to keep his nose out of the dirt, keeps him from the crosshairs of the most powerful gangsters in the city.
Gameplay:
The game is an open-world RPG in much the same feel as Grand Theft Auto. The game features a full city map with expansive options and lots of potential for side-mission fun.
The police is far more vigilant in this game than other like-faced games that I've seen. Even doing something as simple as speeding will get you arrested if you let them, and if you resist arrest, the police can recognize the vehicle you drove in, even your appearance, demanding you to switch vehicles, or even your clothes if you want to lose the heat.
The storyline in this game is a large part of it, and it is indeed an extremely well written story, with impressive voice acting and believable characters. You won't find this game all that enjoyable if you don't like a good mobster story, and this one is exactly that.
Did I mention that this game has porn magazines as an in-world collectible? :p Yep, actual, naked cover girl magazines <3
Graphics:
The physical appeal of the game is considerable. It manages to look believable without suffering in framerate. Anti-Aliasing is available without destroying your ability to play, and shadows are not the usual resource hogging monstrosity that they seem to be in almost EVERY SINGLE GAME. In all considerations possible for the graphics, they are adequate for what they intend to do.
Overall/Random:
If I were to give this game a rating, which I do very rarely, I'd probably give it 8 out of 10 stars. The game is an extremely good, considerable game in the mobster genre, and is entirely capable of holding its own without needing the prequel(I have never even seen gameplay footage of Mafia I before.)
However, it falls short in longivity. The game's story has a beginning, and it most definitely has an end, after which the game feels incredibly dry, boring, and repetitive. The collectibles(sexy as they may be), are not enough to captivate you enough to collect ALL of them unless you're an achievement collector. I'd have definitely given it 9, perhaps even 10, if the publishers could've figured out some way to extend the potential gameplay hours.
Will I recommend this game? Absolutely. I'd say it's worth a play to anyone who likes mobster games. But as I mentioned formerlly: If you want a mobster game where you get to be the 'big boss' ? Don't bother with this one.

I got this game when it was dirty cheap that one time Saints Row 2 was free and played the third game first because I heard that was the best and I had an absolute blast with it. I jumped straight into this one afterwards and wasn't disappointed. It's absolutely over the top and ridiculous, far more ridiculous than the previous one.
Even though I understand people who say it's way too silly and they prefer the more grounded style of three, this game still gave me tons and tons of fun-filled hours of gameplay. If you're not into superpowers and the kinda♥♥♥♥♥♥this game will throw at you then there's nothing I can tell you that will make you enjoy it. But once you've put that behind you, there's tons of stuff this game can offer you.
I was thinking about what I would say about this game while I was playing it and my main ~concern was that it doesn't use its potential to the fullest. There are so many guns and so many powers and it's only rarely that you're forced to use a specific one. I've blasted through huge chunks of the game with just my pistols and the freeze power. I like it when all the toys get used in a game and am often disappointed when most of them are there for just decoration.
Then I realised that this is a sandbox game, obviously it's only as much fun as you make it. With the challenges and activities the game will try to help you explore these opportunities but you're the one with the power, if you can't make this game entertaining and versatile for yourself you're doing it wrong.
One more thing I can say to praise this game is that even though driving is techically obsolete in it, it's actually SO GOOD, like it was in the previous installment of the game, that whenever I noticed my favourite car cruising on the street (Raycaster, whoop-whoop!) I had to stop and steal it so I could drive it to my next objective even if jumping and flying would've been faster. So props for that.
I also found it way easier than the third game. It's either because at one point you become crazy OP (infinite RPG ammo? what the heck? don't you know who I am?) or because your activities are neatly organised in a list that's divided into these personal missions the gang gives you. In the third game it'd often hold me back from doing activities to see "Difficulty: Hard" when hovering above an activity. In this one I didn't even look at what I was going to do, I was just blindly following the waypoint so I could finish another side mission and complete my friends' lists.
At the end of the day Saints Row IV is about one thing above all: fun. Stupid, stupid fun. It's still not better than the third, but I'll definitely be replaying it many, many times.

i played this game before it was on steam. beat it once and did several playthroughs that i didnt finish. (or did i ?)
so nevermind my 5.3 hours on record.
this rpg is very similiar to the deus ex games. a lot of your time will be spend in open "hub"? areas where there is a lot to explore and find.
a lot of places you didnt expect to be there and some disturbing secrets.
combat wise you can shoot, sneak, bash and use bloodmagic and the like. all is mostly stat based.
there are no levels in the game you just get exp that you can spend on anything you like whenever you like. (except for some clan exclusive abilities)
this game is highly NONlinear. there are not only multiple endings but branching storylines and various ways to complete a quest.
want to talk your way through the entire game? well you can. but make sure your vampire clan isnt nosferatu or you will be so hideously deformed that most people will run away from you and call the cops. sometimes you might convince someone you had a horrible accident but you should really stick to the shadows and mostly the sewers where you feed on rats.
want to be part of the insane malkavian clan so you cant speak one coherent sentence and creep everybody out and convince human beings that they are in fact turtles? you can too but prepare for things to unfold very differently. or do you want to be part of the snobbish ruler clan where the lower classes will treat you with disdain or a pretty boy (or gal) who charmes and seduces his way through the game (to the disdain of certain nosferatus).
you can choose to hack computers and talk and find clues to complete quest. or bully, brawl and shoot your way through the questlines. you can be compassionate, insane or cruel all these things shape the story you will experience. not only can you decide the way you approach the game mechanically but you also have a say in how the story unfolds. for better or worse.
there is a lot of atmosphere and humour to the game so there are definitely light hearted moments. but for the most part its all about lowlife, decadence, depravity, perversion and supernatural and sometimes even lovecraftian horror.
bloodlines is using the source engine (the half life 2 one). im not sure but i think it came out before half life 2 and it certainly shows. but the facial animations in the dialouge are on point. ranging from bored teenage store clerk, doped up pawn shop owner or insane cultist. oh and the mutliple choice dialogue is decently expansive. with great writing.
troika went broke while completing the game so it was released in a very buggy state. nonetheless this game was (and still is) considered by many rpg fans as one of the best. i concur. if you like deus ex or just rpgs in general you will find a lot to like. its quite unique and unmatched in many ways. certainly the best vampire game on the market.
even 13 years (wow really? time flies!) after release the community is still active in modding and patching the game. you should definitely (yes there is no argument to be had) get the latest unofficial community patch by wesp (i think) from patchesscrolls. the last one is from a few days ago. shows you the dedication of certain fans. a lot of bugfixes and an optional plus patch that restores content cut from the game due to development limitations and such.
the voice acting ranges from superp and excellent to "sufficient". but the enviromental sounds are quite fitting and the soundtrack gives you a great neonoir (thats a thing right?) feeling.
theres a lot more to mention and im sure other steam reviews will help you out or some big game reviewers go into more detail. all in all its a fantastic game and there is no reason not to try it.

this "low violence" version used to be sold as the german uncut version in stores and it basically is.
the only confirmed cut is a nanosecond of the intro sequence and if you install the unoffical patch "plus" the restoration stuff you dont have to "worry" about that either.

I doubt I'll see anything else like this for as long as I live. That's the true tragedy of V:TMB. As the years pass, and the game industry grows increasingly stagnant and problematic, only the biggest most profitable game franchises can survive. This means that year after year we'll keep seeing the Elder Scrolls, the Call of Dutys, the newest Mario spin, and whatever else; probably Final Fantasy 55 at this point. Point is, a game like this wouldn't even come close to piercing the surface of mainstream interest, let alone acclaim.
So, firstly, enjoyment in this game hinges entirely on how much you like vampires. This game takes after the actual role playing lore and books very closely. That means a lot of weird terminology, specifics, and politicking. Unfortunately, this is where V:TMB runs into problems. Limitations, namely. I can see the vision the creators had, and their dedication to the niddy gritty is appreciated, but the game is held back by itself in a lot of cases. This is a clunker of a game, and I don't think anyone would be able to defend that. Everything feels so... Crude. It just doesn't hold a candle to games that had their engine in better order. Even contemporary or earlier games could handle some of these problems. Inventory management is a chore. Flipping through separate pages for items is a pain. What's worse is the combat, which won't get any mercy from me. It's pretty bad. And not bad in the charming way. Just bad. Things rapidly go downhill after your first fight. Hits lack impact, and the thrill of sending enemies spinning with a three hit combo wears off fast when every enemy in the game does that. Ranged combat fares the same. None of the guns feel especially satisfying to use; aside from maybe the sniper rifle, but that's just from the sheer power of it.
But let's talk about something immediate. This game won't run without a patch. It simply can't understand recent hardware enough to run without a patch. The thing is, this game hasn't been updated at all. The original creators left this game in a state, like a poor abandoned puppy. So, downloading a patch will be your first order of business if you buy this game. Which, I don't know why you would, considering its current year, but whatever.
What about the rest of the game? The characters in general are very convincing for their roles. I wanted to talk to them as much as I could. Customization for the player character isn't what I'd consider modern, but it is very interesting. How you want to play will likely rest on your choice of lineage, or vampire clan. Sidequests on the whole are rewarding. The plot itself is interesting, sure, but falls short on some points. It feels like you get some real choices here. Not only with what kind of ending you want, but also how you want to play, or role play, I should say. I have yet to see another video game that legitimately lets you play an insane person; an insane person that speaks in gibberish riddles no less. Now, whether that's a result of my patch or the base game, I'm not sure, but its impressive nonetheless. This game makes big strides for player freedom, but has limits of its own to worry about. It feels like you're put on story rails, and after a while of playing the main storyline, I'll admit, it got a bit exhausting. It seems like everywhere I turned in this game, it was lacking that extra bit of grandeur it desperately needed. It's a shame.
It's dated. It hasn't aged well. It tries, sure. It chugs along as well as it can. But what goes through my mind when I play this game isn't "wow what a blast from the past," its more like "what would this game look like if it was made today with twice the budget?" This is a true role playing game. There's rolling dice for damage. There's leveling up your stat points, and spending blood points to use any one of your hereditary vampire powers. This is serious nerdery at work here, and I love it, because no other games but the most fringe nerd experiments would embark on this complete transition. Its exceptionally admirable. But apparently it wasn't made to be. Instead we get rpgs that streamline and dumb down formulas. We get games that are rpgs in name only, We get games that fail to bring anything interesting to the table at all.
What I'm saying is, this game is a miracle. For every stilted exchange, there is a cool little sidequest. For every half finished stealth section, there is a piece of interesting lore shown to you. Whatever immovable objects that had to align to make this game possible, I'm thankful for them. It might not be the best or most entertaining game, but damned if its not a piece of gaming history. Unlike Fallout, its unlikely that this franchise will ever see the light of day. But for a quaint little vampire game, that's not too bad.

King Arthur's Gold, or KAG, is one of the few mulitplayer games I have that I will always come back to.  Here are some reasons why:
a) It is fun.  It really is.  There are two main game modes, CTF and Take The Halls which is like your standard CP capture mode.
b)  Buildings collapse if you blow up their supports and there is a basic fluid mechanic in place which means you can flood tunnels.
c) Easy to pick up the basics.  The community is generally very helpful.  If you are in a server and have any questions you will usually get a helpful answer.
d) Runs on a potato.
e) Not too serious.  Want to get over the enemy wall?  Sit in a catapult and get someone to fire you.  Still not clearing it?   Try holding a chicken so you can glide in...
f) This is the most important one for me:  It is one of the VERY few games where if you play well enough, you can turn the tide of the battle and your team can win.  For example, if you are losing but manage to sneak past the enemy and build a tunnel, your team can then start to teleport to that point which can win the match.  But generally speaking the better team will win.
KAG is NOT:
Perfect, there have been glitches and will always be glitches.
Always 100% stable.  If you collapse a MEGA tower, it may crash the server.  Quite rare in my experience.
If you can see past the few issues, there is a gem of a game here.

Divide by Sheep, is a IPA* game, developed by Victor Solodilov and Denis Novikov; published by tinyBuild.
There is a storyline for the game but it isn't much to it nor its' rememberable.
IPA - Indie Puzzle Adventure
I want to mentioned that the visuals for this game is nicely done. The visuals can be adjusted in the option menu.
I want to mentioned that the audio for this game is well done even if it's simplistic and somewhat repetitive. The audio can be adjusted in the option menu as well.
There are no difficult modes to choose from but each of the levels has their own difficulty.
There are five worlds with thirty levels in total six hundred levels. All levels has three stars to earn.
There's an option for resetting the level if an error has been made. All levels can be replayed to earn all three stars. The first world is automatically unlock but the other four worlds are locked. They required a certain amount of stars to unlock them.
New game mechanics are introduced into the game as it progresses. As it being said the puzzles will certainly get tricky to solve.
There nineteen achievements to earned but each has a requirement before they can be unlocked.
There are total of six different trading cards. You only get the three of those cards from the game. There are several ways to get the rest of the trading card: Purchased from Steam's Market; Trade with friends; Booster Packs and it's Booster Pack Creator.
Final thoughts, I've found this game enjoyable to certain extend. The replay value for this game is low. I would recommend this game but not at the full price.

Who said sheeps are always innocent? Divide by Sheep proves that not every sheep is as innocent as the German proverb 'I am innocent like a sheep' says.
The goal of this puzzle game is sending the exact amount of sheeps to the life boat which is given at the start of each level. This is done by using the platforms the wooly animals are standing on and "shooting" them to neighbouring ones. However if the number of sheeps exceeds the space on the platforms, you can watch some sheeps taking a dive into the water. But ofcourse sheeps aren't the only characters you need to complete each level: as soon as you think that you get the gist of this "easy" game, you will meet pigs, wolfs and painful-sheep cutting lasers as well as other mechanis to not only fill life boats but also the ride of the grim reaper.
This game is a good way to get your logical thinking going, if you try to get a perfect completion on every single level. For people who aren't aversed to puzzle games that are repetitive in its main goal and are looking for a time killing challenge, Divide by Sheep is definitely a good game to get their brain cells going without having to rage quit too much. (Better get it on a sale, if you have a chance. Else it might hit the limit you might be willing to offer for a puzzle game you can only complete once without losing the fun)
People who are more disdained to repetitive game play or are expecting a big complex story should probably avoid it.

Harveys New Eyes is the first adventure i have ever played, so I will not (be able to) compare it with other games of this genre. Instead, I will talk about my overall experience with this game.
First of all, a friend showed me this game some time ago and I stored it in my backmind. When it was on sale some weeks ago, I could not resist - and I never regretted this decision!
It is a lovely made, 10 hours long/short adventure with a very...morbid and deep-black sense of humor, hidden behind the eyes of an "innocent", cute little girl. The narrator does its best to keep every mature-only-situation as child-friendly as possible (I can and do only talk about the GERMAN narrator!) which leads to awkward moments...and I really enjoyed them!
There are three VERY different chapters in "Harvey´s New Eyes" and each of them had its unforgettable highlights. For example, in chapter three you become part of a pen-and-paper rpg, which is a small but brand-new, very entertaining situation...
The puzzles - at least for me - are neither too difficult, nor too easy. Some puzzles took me some minutes, but overall I had no moments where I thought that I´d need help or had no more ideas. All puzzles make - kind of - sense and none of them are too far-fetched.
Sadly, this game has some graphical problems, i.e. the items sometimes popped up without the background, when i entered a new screen. In addition, there was a moment when the game broke and I had to load my last savegame.
Overall I highly recommend this game to all people who love this-kind-of-humor!
But what do I really mean with this sentence?
Well..just play the demo!!!
If you like the demo - buy the game!!! (Maybeee...not for 20 bucks...but thats, of course, up to you)
If you dislike the demo - don´t buy it. The demo is veeery close to the kind-of-humor. And the reason to (dis-)like this game...just IS the humor!
Overall I give it a 9/10. And I really hope for a successor.

Ignore the cute artwork - in the first act, you KILL all of your classmates!
This game is DARK! It's morbid humor and I love it! The narrator has that peachy GLaDOS-style negative-spin on everything. The voice acting is great with the dialog as funny as Monkey Island.
The art isn't amazing, but passable. I was never confused by any of the visuals. Having interactable objects 'glow' helps so you're not searching for every little pixel. Like the other reviews, the mouth motions really distract from the clean art. The animations are bad, but that's the only fault I can really find.
The puzzles aren't abstract, and the narrator gives you a lot of tips in solving problems. Some puzzles have you filling out grids, which flew over my head. Luckily, there's a skip button for them. I found myself able to figure out most of the puzzles if I really put my mind on it. I'm not the smartest person, so expert adventure gamers might find the puzzles too easy.

Now. I really liked the atmosphere of this game, but there are a few considerations you have to do before getting it.
The pace of this game is really slow compared to the quick wits of similar games, and the (English) voicing is terrible for some characters.
However... The game has really interesting and original features, and its story worths a go. If you are very much into point-and-click adventures and possibly interesting storytelling you might really like this game. Otherwise I'd advise to simply play the wonderful Deponia, which is overally better.

With this game being so vastly different from the previous ones, I feel like this needs to be said before I get into describing it. Saints Row 4 pretty much detaches itself completely from the its origins of rivalry gangs, and well, a lot of people don't like that. With SR2 being the most praised game of the series, many feel that every following SR game should be in its likeness. I love SR2, but to me, that would've been insanely boring, and I think it's a great thing that the Saints evolved so much from what they were; a disorganized street gang, becoming internationally famous, to saving humanity (kinda).
The humor in this game is great with just the dialogue alone. It has tons of references of miscellaneous things, while not being overdone, as well as references from past SR games. I was thinking about what I would say about this game while I was playing it and my main ~concern was that it doesn't use its potential to the fullest. There are so many guns and so many powers and it's only rarely that you're forced to use a specific one. I've blasted through huge chunks of the game with just my pistols and the freeze power. I like it when all the toys get used in a game and am often disappointed when most of them are there for just decoration.
Then I realised that this is a sandbox game, obviously it's only as much fun as you make it. With the challenges and activities the game will try to help you explore these opportunities but you're the one with the power, if you can't make this game entertaining and versatile for yourself you're doing it wrong.
One more thing I can say to praise this game is that even though driving is techically obsolete in it, it's actually SO GOOD, like it was in the previous installment of the game, that whenever I noticed my favourite car cruising on the street (Raycaster, whoop-whoop!) I had to stop and steal it so I could drive it to my next objective even if jumping and flying would've been faster. So props for that.
I also found it way easier than the third game. It's either because at one point you become crazy OP (infinite RPG ammo? what the heck? don't you know who I am?) or because your activities are neatly organised in a list that's divided into these personal missions the gang gives you. In the third game it'd often hold me back from doing activities to see "Difficulty: Hard" when hovering above an activity. In this one I didn't even look at what I was going to do, I was just blindly following the waypoint so I could finish another side mission and complete my friends' lists.
At the end of the day Saints Row IV is about one thing above all: fun. Stupid, stupid fun. It's still not better than the third, but I'll definitely be replaying it many, many times.

Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines is a very interesting game. Despite the lacking graphics, really basic combat system, and bugs, there's something awfully enjoyable about it. Whether you're interested in playing as a crazed bloodthirsty maniac, a mysteriously intelligent creature of the night, or even just your typical dark and violent vampire, this game has got you covered. Although there's no indepth character creation, Vampire: The Masquerade allows you to choose your gender, your "clan", and in classic RPG fashion, lets you allocate points earned throughout the game to develop skills of your choice. The level of customization and autonomy given to the player ingame is refreshing,  especially for a game of this sort. The many possible playing styles, dialogue options and etc. give the game great potential for replayability.
Overall, Vampire: The Masquerade is a solid, fun game. So long as you don't go in expecting a ground-breaking story or exceptional graphics and combat, you're sure to enjoy the experience.
(PS. Be sure to download the unofficial patch online, since otherwise the game will be unplayable!)

Would i recommend the game?
Yes and no
Yes:
Engine is good and stable and it can handle the units really well.
Stock campaign actually has a good story behind it as well as a built in feature to guide new players into learning the game.
Yes there is "bad language" in but in all honesty, the troopers would of been swearing their heads off anyway.
The rank system where you play games, earn points and then every so often it drops a item for you. That works out nicely as it get players to want to play the game. It also gives you some supply which is used to buy things out of the in-game store. You can also buy things from that store with your money.
Model details are very nice
Customisable skills and skins etc is also a nice touch.
No:
The campaigns are fun and all but come to the skirmish mode for both online and against the AI, that is where it is lacking badly.
The lack of units and the lack of a decent veterancy system (will cover that later on in the review) is poor. The veterancy system is pretty pathetic and i would honestly have rather have seen veteran units in the game that could be built over the system that was put it.
While the game is historically based, it isn't accurate as it should be. I had a vanilla game where the AI pulled out a Tiger 1 so with that, I had to use what i had available to deal with it which so happened to be several Shermans (i brought all the DLC). The 75mms was doing some what would be considered "okish" damage in other games considering what they are against the Tiger 1. Somewhat poor representation of what it was actually like.
I also found the other nations was lacking in units too.
I do what to stress that while this section looks alot, it really isn't as bad as it can come across.
Other:
I havn't played the tutorial of the game so i can't comment on that.
I had an issue where i was trying to make the mods appear in the list (long story) but i had to eventually wipe steam off my HDD and redownload everything. At the time of writing, i'm still downloading the game again so i don't know if that problem still persists. I do however suspect it is a steam issue rather than a game issue.
DLC:
A good amount of DLC. The major nations that fought in late war are represented here in a good fashion as well as having some really good voice overs in the different accents. Be advised that the Oberkommando West is the "late war" varient of the standard german army in the game already. The Oberkommando West is also total pain in the♥♥♥♥♥♥to try and figure out unfortuantly but when you do, you really don't have much to work with however what you do get for an army is very powerful.
Mod Support:
Great mod support. There are many mods out there on the workshop for you to try out and some are really good. The single mod that i would recommend is what i call Operation Spearhead only due to the fact that it sounds much cooler that the title but thats just me:
This mod totally rebuilds the skirmish mods from the ground up. It also adds in many more units, makes players choose different paths for each army including all DLC armies. It replaces the poor vanilla veterancy system with a new one with what it should of been in the first place. All units now get to rank 5 and get better and better i.e faster reloading, further sight etc etc but also do unlock the upgrades they would of done as soon as they get to the rank required.
Conclusion:
I would honestly say that if you can live with using this mod to play the game then do so. If your a vanilla fan then eh...i'd look elsewhere for your money. That said, this game has a lot to give and it also had a lot of potential that was lost. The game is 23gb with all DLC included but excluding mods. It will take a while to download and i'll cut out all the DLC which should bring it down to somewhere between 15-19gb without any DLC. I feel that 15gb for what you get in the game including a load of skirmish maps which are the ones in the campaign is very big for what it is which does seem to me that the game wasn't compressed? Who knows. Relic will be the chaps to answer that question
So, where does that leave us?
Mod Support: 8/10
DLC: 6/10 (Mod support: 8/10)
Vanilla Game: 5/10
It had so much potential but had so much lacking. I can promise that when you get your head around how the Spearhead mod works, then play with that mod for a while, go back to vanilla game. You'll see how lacking the game is and its a toal shame.
As of 12/11/16, the game is £19.99. Is it worth it? Yes if you want a good storyline but only get this if/when its on sale. I will keep playing this game only if the Spearhead mod is still functioning or another damn good mod is working. If not then i won't play the game anymore.
Note, Spearhead mod does NOT affect the campaign. Only skirmish games against friends and AI. Vanilla game is only available for public matchmaking games as far as i can tell. Could be wrong on that

Hack, Slash, Loot is a Roguelike RPG, meaning that you start with a new character every time and play until you die or win, gaining little except for skill between playthroughs.
HSL has a high learning curve, which is a problem since the game tells you nothing about how to play. The interface does nothing to help. It took me about ten deaths to figure out how to do well enough to live for more than a few minutes. It takes a lot of time and research to play HSL effectively, but once you know some of the basics, the game becomes more fun.
What HSL does right is removing the player's inventory. You only carry what you have equipped. Everything else is dropped or used. This simplifies the mechanics a lot and streamlines play. The downside is that I found the mechanics to be a little shallow for a Roguelike, and much of your success depends on luck. The game is very poorly balanced.
HSL isn't the best Roguelike, but there's fun to be found. It's worth getting if you find it on sale.

If you love a well-made platformer, I would recommend this--I think it, along with VVVVVV and Knytt Underground, have the most replay value of the platformers I own (it has an overall atmosphere that I enjoy--I can play it on a weekend night for relaxing entertainment). And like those other two games, the soundtrack is really well crafted.
I would compare the difficulty of this game to VVVVVV: it's generally moderately difficult, but with a couple spots (for me, the spitting prawns, a room with fireballs and snakes, and one particularly tricky moving platform surrounded by spikes with a flying bat overhead) that are quite challenging. All in all, I think it's well designed and balanced.
I purchased Super Win the Game, and actually don't like it as well (although I still really enjoy SWtG).
Ultimately, it's free. If you enjoy retro platformers, why wouldn't you check it out?

Mafia 2 is basically a GTA clone in the 1940s-50s. Thats the most essential single sentence description I could give. Clones arn't necessarily a completely bad thing. But unlike GTA, staples of GTA are missing from this game. Staples of the third person open world genre in general are missing which is dissappointing.
Gameplay- This is a third person cover combat oriented open world game. Though in the open world theres really nothing to do. Many open world games suffer from this and open world just ends up being what you drive past in between missions and going from A to B. I did find that NPCs are entertaining in this game. They will slip on ice and fall, crash into eachother and start fighting, and if the police are near they might even end up getting arrested or getting killed execution style because the cops don't like it when you run. (Police brutality dousn't exist in this world as dead people don't make complaints) There are various stores spread out through the world but they have very little in the way of goods, Even the gun stores are pretty lacking considering as most of the stores in general are just copy pasted. The special places like Harveys Surplus and the junkyard are pretty far from the rest of the world so it does take a bit longer than it would have been nice to get to and back from these areas. Outside of buying items and upgrading vehicles you don't do anything in between missoins. Sure you can rob stores and crush cars for money but you will never want or need to do this outside of when the game makes you do it to get enough cash.
The game is pretty realistic in its portrayal of the time period. This is when the USA was on top of the world and her people were at the peak of wealth and happiness I feel and it shows in the world but it can be hard to see if you don't know much about the US history of modern times. There are traffic laws you must obey such as speed limit, having an accident , or basically running into anything or anyone will get the police on you if they are near and see it. Going above 40MPH will end you up with a $50 ticket if you pull over. This gets annoying as heck as time goes on but thankfull they don't seem to care if you run a redlight but if Joe is in the car with you he cares ironically. It really gets annoying when you just want to get to the next mission and the police end up on your tail due to going to fast just so you could get where you needed. Cars handle realistically like boats as you would expect for this time period and its great! Theres a decent variety of cars too and some are quite sporty and nimble compared to the rest. Guns handle as atleast in character of the real counterparts which is better than I could have probably asked for. If it wasn't for the flawed damage system the game would really make you feel like a Mobster.
The health/damage system is absolutely atroucius and it becomes more of an issue as you progress. Remember I called this a cover based shooter? I wasn't joking. Later in the game you spend more time popping out of cover then staring at walls than you could ever wan't. While I like the idea of a cover system I hate when its forced onto me because its just not fun to pop out of cover and in to let my health regen. As the enemies are freaking crazy with their accuracy at any range and their fire rate too you have to be insanely skillfull and carefull to not get killed. Some enemies will literally balls to the walls run at you with a Thompson with a drum mag and just dump you the whole time. When 2 or more enemies do this and your stuck to cover the game can be to clunky to let you really defend yourself, especially with a controller (as I feel every TPS is better with a controller for the most part). It would have been nice to have a health system with more leeway as you just die to easily on normal especially in the later parts of the game where good cover may not be avaliable. There is no armor avaliable or atleast I didn't find any and if you at any point lose health you can only regen to 75% or so HP and you have to eat something to get back to 100%. Its just very asinine and some of the areas do not compliment the cover based style very much especially when the enemy AI is fairly stupid and enjoys rushing you.  I wanted to play the game like Max Payne which is superiour in the fun and in design of how it handles cover and health. No painkillers and only pain and ham for Vito.
The cover system like the health system sucks, You can get shot even when your behind cover and it can be difficult to know why or how you could have avoided it as parts of your character can stick out. I mean really small parts and the enemies with their stupid accuracy hit these small areas making for a very frustrating experience even when you try to play the game the way the devs meant especially when the enemies really like just running up on your and popping you. Did I also mention that theres no blindfire? In a cover based game with full auto guns? Also you can't shoot and drive nor can you jump out of a vehicle. The latter isn't as much of a problem as the former. The gameplay can be quite fun weilding these historic guns you can't even legally think about in parts of the USA anymore.
Some areas compliment the gameplay/combat design very well though and these are high points in the game that are to rare. Times when you don't have a friendly armed NPC to watch your back (thankfully they are invuln) the game becomes alot less fun as its even more easy for NPCs to rush you. The well designed areas are primarily the last missions or so and the early missions, I feel. Much of that inbetween was very frustrating.
All in all driving is fun, the combat is only sometimes fun and too difficult as I feel the difficulty just makes the game longer instead of making the experience challenging and rewarding, but theres some features missing that probably shouldn't be and it does feel like a clone albeit with its own coat of paint to the GTA style of game.
Story wise, I was a bit confused for much of the middle and end game. It seems like you keep going through similiar scenarios and events that should be pretty big and volatile are relatively short lived and pass. The burning of the home and attempted murder of Vito is one thing that I felt should have carried a little more weight than it did. All you end up doing is going out and killing all the people that were behind it in one mission than thats over and your homeless and broke because vito had no insurance and all his cash was apparently in his mattress. I felt like this sort of thing had already happened once or twice already and that feeling happened quite a bit in this game. It was confusing as to who was who and who was working for who and the whole story felt pretty crappy around or after the time the house is burnt. There didn't feel like there was a really strong underlying theme like in some games or that any character was really dynamic. Vito is a killing machine. Nothing like Niko Belic who talks deeply at times but knows he has to do what he does for reasons while Vitos main reasoning is "what else would I do?" even though hes relatively young and wealthy at times and could get a decent education and a real job. He even knows that the lifestyle hes living isn't good so it dousn't make much sense as to why he keeps hammering away at it. GTA4 and Niko don't get enough credit for the story as it holds some pretty deep stuff in it and the character while this game and Vito are pretty 2d and even when they arn't they are flat as a peice of paper.
Graphics look really good and its cool to see the period and the sound isn't to bad either aside from the occasional VO that dousn't sound like it came from the character. To many songs on the three radio stations suck though.
I know this review is fairly negative but for a GTA clone set in the Mafia days this isn't so bad. I did enjoy some aspects. Not worth $30 tho.

Great crime noir, great story, great gameplay.
One of my favorite games, Mafia 2 is a wonderful crime drama set in the late 30's and early 40's. Unfortunately, the player doesn't ever make decisions for Vito, but that's understandable in a shooter. The stroyline is great and the dialogue is immersive. I've had a lot of fun driving around the city listening to old music, shooting up clothing stores, getting into shootouts with the police. To be honest though, I have no idea how I've sunk so much time into this.
I really enjoy the open world, however it's pretty barebones. You can buy food which heals you, clothes that disguise you, and... well that's about it. You can repaint cars as well to lose police but it's easier to just find a new car. I think you can also purchase gas? I've only done that once in all my time of playing. You earn money for doing jobs but the money seems pretty pointless, especially considering there are points in the story where you lose everything anyway.
As I've said numerous times, the story is great. Who doesn't move a good crime drama every once in a while? Italian men smoking in bars, car chases, shooting out windows with a tommy. This game does a great job of capturing the feel of being a 40's gangster. The Voice acting is pretty solid throughout, and the music is incredibly immersive and an absolute joy listening to.
While they are still very nice, the graphics haven't aged that perfectly. Don't get me wrong, they're still incredible but after a few years issues start to pop up. Low res models for anyone but the main cast always bothers me. But this is incredible nit picky isn't it? The enviroment feels very alive and full of energy (Just don't follow the civillians too closely) and the animations... Oh man, the character animations are great, fantastic even. During cutscenes the characters move around so, so well. And I smile with glee every time vito's head moves around when I get shot at.
Gameplay, the meat and potatoes of shooters. The gunplay is pretty solid, with only a few issues here and there. My major problem with the gameplay isn't the game's fault, but my own. After spending so much time playing I've gotten too good for the AI to be difficult, and I can make almost any shot with any gun. An option to disable the annoying crosshair would be nice. Also, a blindfire mechanic would fit nicely. But I still have fun loading up sometimes and throwing molotoves at a clothing store then shooting up the windows before driving away.

I think where this developer went wrong is making people expect something that it isn't .
Saying "survive the horrors" makes people think its a survival horror game- it's not.
Saying "Make It Indie! is an indie game about making an indie game." makes you think you will be constructing some sort of game as part of the game. You don't.
Saying "Over 30 minutes of HD videos that immerses the player" makes you think it will be artistically beautiful and atmospheric. It isn't.
Saying "An intuitive gameplay experience." makes you think you're going to be introduced to some unique gameplay mechanics. It doesn't.
Saying "Truly diverse music tracks." makes you think you're going to hear some engaging and immersive game music. You don't.
Saying "P.S. Don't take this game too seriously!" doesn't change much.
If you set your people up to think the game is something completely different than it is, you're setting yourself up for a lot of disappointed and negative reviews. The game in itself, while it is very arthouse and probably not to everyone's taste, has nothing really wrong with it. It's just that people were expecting something very different.
Be more accurate in describing your next game and the people who do choose to buy your game will most likely be positive, as it will have been aimed at the right audience.

I've been playing a ton on steam for a few years now. This is by far the worst game that I've played thus far.
The localization is horrible. The game looks to have been designed for Russian or Ukrainian users or something (Forgive my ignorance on those specifics). In 2015 you should just be able to get translation to American English to work correctly.
The game also implies that you'll be privy to the developers nightmares during the night. Boy what a charmed life one must lead for those to be considered nightmares.
Normally I wouldn't harp on length of a game but the community section claims this game can be completed in 3-5 minutes with 100% achievements (If you skip the cutscenes). I played through normally once and a second time skipping the "nightmare" scenes and it took me 30 minutes to achieve the perfect.
By far the worst part of this experience is that there isn't any fun to be had. I believe this type of experience still has a place in games but this iteration simply has nothing to offer. You'll watch boring cutscene after cutscene of cats being cute, walking down the road, rain falling, someone drawing a picture on a damaged wall for some reason, & more. An odd thought occurred to me while watching some of the scenes. Real peoples faces are displayed from footage taken in public. This is something I can't help but wonder about the legality of including in your for profit game (without the consent of others).
All in all I'd give this a big thumbs down for quality & experience. It's only redeeming quality is some easy achievements.

I bought Edna and Harvey’s New Eyes by mistake. It was bundled with another Daedalic game that I wanted, but I decided to give it a try and 1 hour into gameplay I concluded that if this game manages to keep similar brilliant mood and humor to the final credits, I will madly fall in love with it. In the end it didn’t, but still it is my favorite game from this studio so far. Now, that you know my opinion on the subject, let me tell you that you really should not read this mini-review since perhaps this game is best approached like a typical Daedalic point and click …
…still reading this? …
…you’ve been warned…
…because  it is not the studio’s most typical game.  Sure it retains all the mechanisms this genre is known for, still it seems to be bad at what most Daedalic games are good (2d art) and brilliant at everything else .
The game’s story, narration and voice acting are among the strongest I’ve seen in a point and click during the last few years.  I won’t describe the plot here (not to tell too much, and you’ve got it covered on the game’s Store Page). Instead let me focus on the narration. While Lilly ( the protagonist) does not say a single word throughout the entire game (or does she … ?) the narrator does an OUTSTANDING job constantly commenting on her actions and motives, brilliantly combining the innocence of child’s perspective with the games quite sadistic sense of humor.
Regrettably, the game’s 2nd and 3rd chapters feel slightly weaker than the beginning and conclusion.  As far as I know the game has three endings (two of them good, while the third one … truly awesome). A very strong 8 out of 10.
PL
Ednę i Harvey’a kupiłem przez przypadek. Był w paczce z inną grą z Daedalic w którą chciałem zagrać, zdecydowałem się jednak dać jej szansę i po pierwszej godzinie miałem wrażenie że jeżeli gra utrzyma atmosferę i humor do napisów końcowych, zakocham się w niej bez pamięci. Nie udało się, ale mimo to stała się moją ulubioną pozycją ze studia Daedalic (a ukończyłem już kilka…). A teraz, skoro już znasz moją opinię najlepiej zrobisz nie czytając dalej tej mini-recki bo w Harvey’s New Eyes gra się  najlepiej kiedy spodziewasz się typowo Daedalicowej przygodówki …
..dalej to czytasz?...
..ostrzegałem…
… bo Edna and Harvey nie jest do końca typowym dla tego studia point and clickiem. Zachowuje wszystkie mechanizmy właściwe tego typu grom, ale grafika odstaje od tego do czego przyzwyczaili graczy ludzie z Daedalic’a. Za to voice acting (zazwyczaj tragiczny w grach tych twórców) jest jednym z najlepszych jakie słyszałem od lat, muzyka idealnie pasuje do klimatu gry (rewelacyjny temat z napisów końcowych!) zagadki są ciekawe, pomysłowe … i bywają trudne (niektóre zwyczajnie przekombinowane, inne po prostu rewelacyjne).
Fabuły nie będę zdradzał (a co, jest opisana na stronie gry) powiem tylko że razem z narracją stanowią największą zaletę tej gry. Lilly (postać sterowana przez gracza) nie wypowiada nawet słowa  (chociaż … nie, nic nie powiem! ), za to narrator ciągle komentuje jej poczynania i intencje. I trzeba powiedzieć że robi to w sposób naprawdę GENIALNY. Narracja zgrabnie łączy niewinność perspektywy z jakiej patrzy dziecko z (BARDZO) morderczym humorem jakim ocieka gra.
Szkoda że rodział drugi i trzeci są odrobinę słabsze od pierwszego i rewelacyjnego finału gry (z tego co udało mi się odkryć są trzy zakończenia: dwa solidne i jedno … doskonałe). Podsumowując: bardzo solidne 8/10.

As a fan of the original Edna And Harvey: The Breakout, I was really looking forward to playing the new game. I can tell you that I was not disappointed. The humour, quirky characters, vibrant art style and catchy music that made the first game such a delight are all back in spades.
If you've played the Deponia series, you have probably already played this game. If not, I don't know what's stopping you! Also, if you're a fan of games like Monkey Island, I recommend this game. If you get frustrated easily, this may not be the game for you, as there were a few times where I had to explore and experiment before I could continue. But the objectives from section to section were usually well sign posted, and I hardly ever felt lost and unsure about what I was supposed to do, which leaves the emphasis on the puzzles.
If you're wondering where this fits in with the original game (something I was unsure about when I started playing), it does indeed take place after The Breakout. However, Edna is really a support character in this game, which focusses on a new character, Edna's friend Lili. While it's fun to see these new characters interacting with old favourites (Droggeljug!), it's also good to see new locations added. I would definitely recommend playing the first game before picking this one up, however this game can easily be played without the knowledge of the first game - some of the characters make references to the actions of the first game, and it just makes these references easier to get if you've played the first game. This game feels like it's a bit longer than the first game. There are three sections to the game, with the first taking up about half the game. In fact, I thought the first section was the entirety of the game, and was pleasantly surprised when the second chapter started!
My main gripe about that game would be that it's a bit disappointing that you can't get it on iPad. I played the original on my iPad and the point and click adventure genre is a great way to pass the time on the way to work. Also the controls are quite good, and I find myself pressing the Spacebar in other adventure games hoping to see all the hotspots I can click before having to remind myself that not all adventure games are built this intuitively!
All in all, I enjoyed this game a lot. Not perhaps a classic that will live throughout the ages like the Money Island series, it's still interesting and quirky enough to bring a smile to my face. If you consider yourself a point and click adventure game connoisseur, you need to give the Edna and Harvey series a try. I really hope there's an Edna And Harvey 3!

Well this is a perfect example of not judging a book by it's cover. Usually I'm a huge graphic/visual snob, but when I saw that Daedalic had put forth this quirky and let's be honest, cheap looking game, I did a double take. I bought the game on sale and ladies and gentleman...
This game is kickass.
The story, the characters, the plot, and the unique game play was all FREAKIN AMAZING, FUNNY, AND ORIGINAL. The whole game embodies the term "dark comedy". Yes it's a point and click, but a point and click where you playfully murder bad children? The best part is halfway through the game, you think it's just going to continue being a point and click + murders + a few puzzles, but then it changes!

(Side note: there is a prequel that I haven't even played yet, but I still loved and understood the plot in this game)

It's really interesting how a very simple concept can make something highly engrossing, and One Way Heroics is a good example of this in play. Take a very basic turn based movement and combat system, simplified stats and gear usage, and rather basic 'save the world' story as their parts, and this isn't anything new nor special by any degree, yet once you add in the ever moving 'Darkness', a mass of black that's always moving ahead, with or without you activly running away from it, and it suddenly becomes this odd pressured race of time and land management.
The main key point is whever you take an actions, yet it be attack or talking or even moving, the darkness moves a bit as well, devouring that part of the map with it making it no longger accessible. Suddenly you might be trying to rush towards a small city outpost hoping to sell your overload of loot, only to get there to watch the vender NPC's parish in that very second, having to now make a rush forward hoping another isn't too far off. It suddenly makes every little action you do feel 'importent' in the grand scale of things, and it really forces you to learn to look out for selective map alterations, or carry around Map Scrolls to ensure you don't miss anything vital. The NPC's you can recrute as well also have  rather small, but kinda interesting storylines, each one giving a bit more clear overarching idea of just what's going on, and perhaps a way to really 'save the world'. Not to ruin anything, but those who explore and read up will chances are find far more then this game first lets on.
On top of all of this, is a small, but nifty option of online interactions. It's nothing Dark Souls worthy of jolly co-op and the like, but it's more say little snapshots into other's current playing situations as they trek on the same world, able to share a small snipit of text, and be shown how they are status wise. Of course, on death, you can also share something much the same, and depending on where you died, your ghost might help someone else's journey along, dropping a random peice of loot you had at the moment. Beyond all of that, it's a nice, addicting, and simple game you can pick up for an hour or two, feel like you've made some progress, and seems to always have just ONE more little thing to show you even many hours after the fact.

I do not know what to say, so here is a recipe for soup with meat.
Hearty Beef and Barley Soup Recipe
TOTAL TIME: Prep: 20 min. Cook: 1 hour 50 min. MAKES: 9 servings
Ingredients
1 pound beef top round steak, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
1 tablespoon canola oil
3 cans (14-1/2 ounces each) beef broth
2 cups water
1/3 cup medium pearl barley
1 teaspoon salt
1/8 teaspoon pepper
1 cup chopped carrots
1/2 cup chopped celery
1/4 cup chopped onion
3 tablespoons minced fresh parsley
1 cup frozen peas
Directions
1. In a Dutch oven, brown beef in oil; drain. Stir in the broth, water, barley, salt and pepper. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat; cover and simmer for 1 hour.
2. Add the carrots, celery, onion and parsley; cover and simmer for 45 minutes or until meat and vegetables are tender. Stir in peas; heat through.
Yield: 9 servings (2-1/4 quarts).
Nutritional Facts
1 cup: 128 calories, 3g fat (1g saturated fat), 28mg cholesterol, 466mg sodium, 10g carbohydrate (2g sugars, 3g fiber), 14g protein.
This hearty barley soup is a favorite menu item in our house throughout the year. Everyone savors the flavor. —Elizabeth Kendall, Carolina Beach, North Carolina
