The good: Random, roguelike play, text based rpg aspects, no two games are alike. Unlocks, and varations on how you set up your ships (I don't mean the layouts but after you start) lead to much replayability.
The bad: The game does everything it can to make you miserable and or lose. Before the expansion this was also true but not quite so vehemently. The end boss even on easy is impossible for me but apparently some people have solved it. After 64 hours I am giving up on it. Even with Advanced mode off the game is 10x harder than it was. Getting near my scores of several years ago is severely challenging in a bad way. Sometimes it feels like a run through is a complete waste of time.
The ugly: What do you want for cheap? The game is too hard for people who aren't willing to dedicate their lives to solving it. I suspect being under 40 years old helps (because lets face it us old folks just aren't as 'smart' as we used to be.) And having the patience of job probably doesn't hurt either. The game has no frills graphics which I like but may be unexciting for those raised on MMOs and fancy gizmos.
Overall: There is plenty of fun in it and I would recommend it for anyone who doesn't mind losing. All the time. Where you lose in the game will vary and much of the time it won't seem like you have much control over it. Even if you are great at multitasking and micromanaging the challenges are insurmountable. This is the nature of Rogue's descendents. Even those set in space. Except for the ones that are more 'like-lite' than 'like'.
As they say the meaning is in the journey not in the destination so play it and revel in the many fiery deaths you get to experience.
Unlocking ships is a mini game that can be fun if you get very lucky. I've managed 4 in 4 years so hey. Advanced edition offers more things to confound, amuse and mystify you. (New races, items, ships, etc)
Don't be embarrassed to play on easy and don't forget to look for help because the game is designed to be ultra hard even on the easy mode. (There are people who will need to show their epine by claiming otherwise but ignore them. The truth is you learn in baby steps and die repeatedly, horribly and without mercy. You do get to do pretty mean things to others while doing so, so there is that.)
Especially learn what the basics of the game are and then learn the basic 'no nos' because that will get you pretty far. Sector 8 is not hard to get to (though intact may be a different story) once you've managed to get to sector 5 which is not hard to get to once you learn how to get through sectors without being blown randomly. And then you get to learn how to die to the Rebel Flagship. If not in the first battle then in the next or the last. Only the lucky and skillful survive the final battle. I am neither so far.

I enjoy playing this game from time to time, even though I kinda suck at it (or maybe it's just my team, I haven't found out a good way to tell which one it is yet).
Unfortunately I find it very difficult to recommend because of the monetization choices made by the devs. You'd think it was a free-to-play title. $4 for vehicle skins, about the same amount for "victory strikes", faceplates for your player card, and these things that amount to perks for your faction.
And then there's the ones that everyone complains of: A fairly large amount of cash for the commanders, which basically dictate your playstyle. So if you want to use the flavor-of-the-month "OP" commanders for that given week or whatever, or even if you want to play the game a different way, (especially considering some of these "perks" I mentioned earlier require some of the units you can only get by using these premium commanders) you either need to stump up the green and pay the piper, or you have to grind for days (And I mean days, it IS an RTS after all) for the in-game currency. And that trickles in at, from what I know, 500 per level-up. That's not much, considering you need like 25k at least or so to get these commanders. But again, you COULD just dump real money into them. Which gives you the same thing as if you had ground for days. This keeps coming up in my games and it's disappointing, it just makes taking time to get to know the game's ins-and-outs worthless. Why try when you can just pay for everything? Oh right, because you could buy an entire 'nother game with that money.
Speaking of which... yeah, I can't in good conscience say this is a good buy. ♥♥♥♥ing... ten bucks or so for a Sturmtiger. That's just baiting.
Edit: For the record, I looked up a forum thread or two on "Warspoils Farming", or farming the system that gives you your after-game drops. What I found was... hilarious. Basically, without explaining, one of the Lelic moderators was parading around and threatening bans for anyone who tried farming with mods or scripts (the most efficient way to do things). In other words, if you try to "abuse the system" to get at all the content in the game WITHOUT getting shilled, they will remove your ability to play the game. Is that even legal?

Awkward Dimensions Redux, in the simplest of terms, is a very pretty, artsy walking sim with a comentary on game development as a whole. For me, and I'm sure for many others, it is more than a 'Walking Sim'. TL;DR at the bottom.
POSITIVES
+Free
+Pretty
+Great OST
NEGATIVES
-Short
-'In your face' Artsy
-Had some issues with controls
-Sometimes confusing directionally.
My Opinion:
Overall, 100% worth downloading. I mean, it's free for christ's sake. The OST is worth your time downloading alone. This game delivers many messages within the span of an hour of play. Messages vary from player treatment of game devs to the pressures society place upon young and aspiring students to succeed. These messages are driven home by the atmosphere and often emotional 'commentary' from the developer. Not "The Beginners Guide" style commentary, but idle ramblings or rants that the player gets a peek of. MOST people will find one or two messages that get to them. (I know I did)
RAMBLINGS AHEAD
This has been officially placed on my list of "Games that make an argument for themselves being art." Because, whether you like it or not, this game very much IS art. Same with "The Beginners Guide", these games are impactful. They tell an important story. A story of a struggling developer who wants to get their message out, but has no means to. Games like this one are vital to the evolution of the games industry as a whole. They prevent the perverting of the industry into nothing more than "GTA COD MURDUR PARTY SIMULATOR 20XX" They give people who genuinely care about the industry an example to point to whenever the media paints us as the villain.
TL;DR: 9/10. Short. Pretty. Artsy. Emotional at times. Brilliant OST. Download, play, enjoy.
If nothing else, it's good for some nice wallpapers.

Lost Girl`s [diary] is a purely kinetic novel developed and publised by SmoleVN, whilst the art style and music serves its purpose adequately the story itself whether it be due to poor translation or poor writing while likely fail to keep your attention during the hour the game is stated to last.
Whilst there are some layers of interest within the story such as the unusual beginning making the viewer question if the entire kinetic novel is a in universe story about a group of people telling bad stories or if the events in hotel are supposed to have happen, the majority of the stories within the game sound like attempts at scary stories that young teenages would tell each other. With typical claims to it having happened, all the stories occuring at a camp and generally massive glaring plotholes which every character in the kinetic novel seems to over look until (in rare cases) its pointed out to them.
The problem I find the most with the game is it akin to waiting in a room with annoying strangers that are ignoring you making small talk, its unengaging, occasionally anoying and ultimately you wish you were somewhere else.


Honestly I would advise you spend your time playing one of the better free kinetic or visual novels available on Steam unless you are desperate for achievements, if your curious about the game then you can see my playthrough below and actually hear me growing increasingly annoyed and weary with the game as I progress.

The only bad side is that you are forced to avoid most combat if you want the good ending. Should rather be tied to moral choices and mostly avoiding combat rather than forcing you to turn in to a pacifist in a world where you fight for survival.
Otherwise it is a great story of human survival in a post-apocalyptic future.
An important part of the game is when you come from the deadly tunnels to the stations which have turned in to the last sanctions of humanity. This creates a stark contrast to how bad things really are and provides the player with respit from the extremely dark and hostile world.

I turned my wrist to see my clock, and it was giving me about 7 minutes left of oxygen, I couldn`t see the numbers very well, because of the sweat I was constantly wiping with my hands, I didn`t have any other filter that let me breath outside in the nuclear blasted air, I couldn't find any around me, or in the precarious houses in which walls had crumbled by the wind that blows stronger than never, and I certainly didn`t have the time to search for it. I saw the station I needed to go down, guarded by heavily-armed enemies, and I thought: What am I going to do? Am I going to die and return to the last checkpoint? And if it comes to that, am I going to be stuck in this loop and the game be broken?
I decided I had to go forward, count my bullets because it was as plenty as my oxygen filters, and fight my way through it with any strategy I could be able to plan in that situation. I managed to stealth kill one enemy with my knife, I searched him for filters, but he was on his last one too. I was dragging myself between old cars towards the station, untill the floodlights turned at me and they began shooting. I killed one enemy that rushed at me with a shotgun trying to put an end to that threat (me), but it didn`t took long since the demons started swarming my enemies, and me.
I then saw the machine-gunner being taken away by the demons, and was at that point I realized it was time to take a chance and run for the metro station, risking taking a shot or flown off and swinged by demons.
I made it, I was safe and could take my mask off. I spent a wise one bullet to kill the enemy with the shotgun back there, and that's good, because I don't know what I'm going to face in my journey to the D6, or how many bullets I will need to kill whatever comes to kill me.
Because I succeeded, I didn't have the chance to see what would happen if I died back there. Was I going to return to the last checkpoint, be stuck in that loop, and the game would be broken? I do not know. But what I know, is that the game also succeeded in dragging me into that world, and making me feel what is like to be there.

Ok. It's time. I was going to write this review at 15 hours, but then you know.
I used to play this game for HOURS as a kid. It was a terrible shame when my Battlefront and Battlefront 2 disks for the PS2 got scratched, I survived though. Then I saw that there was a remake (is that what you call it?) on Steam, I thought back to "Our reinforcements our dwindling!" I knew I had to get this, and I was right. If you play through the Campaign Mode AND the Galactic Conquest it's easily 17-20 hours of gameplay. Strangely the 'Instant Action" mode seems less appealing on the PC, but it's still fun. With all the replay value, there's probably a solid 40 hours here.
Now the graphics still look good to this day even with the crazy GTX 9001 stuff, (I have no knowledge whatsoever with graphics cards) making it an even better experience. Now I must say the cancellation of BF3 ticked me off, I actually was one of the very few who got to play it, but it was on the DS. This is honestly the best oldy-but-goody, and it just makes me sad that other children don't know about this amazing experience. All they care about is the latest CoD games, it even makes me sad that alot of kids haven't watched Star Wars! For goodness' sake! I have NEVER encountered a bug in this game AT ALL, not in PS2 nor on the PC, making it automatically run better than most modern games. I seriously don't understand how this game could be hated/disliked by ANYONE. Now I don't really judge sound too much in games, but the soundtrack is great, wether it's the the "defeat" song (dun dun dunnn) or if it's the happy triumphant music of victory, either way the explosions and blaster shots sound great.
The storyline of this game places you not in the place of a rebel warlord or even a member of the rebellion, but a soldier of the 501st legion. (Empire) It really shows the galaxy of Star Wars from an entire different standing, and I and so many others love that change, so it's time to wrap this up.
With all of that off I give this a good 7/10.
I hope you didn't think I was serious, did you? This hidden gem will always have a place in my heart. 10/10, couldn't have done it better.

Mafia II is an open-world game set in the mid 20th century; the game has two distinctive periods, WWII and the early 1950's.
In the first period of Mafia II, I wouldn't call it "fun", but it was immersive, you're in the dark world of criminal organizations in the city of Empire Bay and all you're doing is just dodging bullets with a leather jacket.
In the second period, things get better; as WWII ended and the US reaches prosperity, but you're still dodging bullets, except with a hawaiin shirt.
The cutscenes are smooth and nice, and the voice acting is excellent.

What a great action game, it's like the game itself could become a movie. There's nothing about the mafia way of life that this game doesn't portray such as robbery, murder, blowing money on cars, suits, guns and even speeding tickets.
The gameplay is as simple as any third person shooter, but the environment of the 1940's-1950's really makes it stand out, you even take part in the war, and hear reports about its progress as you play, adding to the game's immersion.
The graphics and music are great aswell, but the game's advantage over other third person shooters is it's story, packed with crime, great personalities and amazing character backgrounds.
Mafia 2 is totally worth the money, it's surely one of the best action games i ever player.

LISA or LISA: The Painful RPG is a beautiful combination between comedy and fear. A lot of the game is very humorous with plenty of funny characthers and moments, all the while the main story is really a brutal and scary journey. Before starting this great story you should probably get some background information on the internet. Because the game follows a characther who was influenced by the events in the first game: LISA: The First. Just look up who LISA was and then you'll understand why Brad is depressed as hell, because they never really mention it in the story.
STORY:
The story is great. It is about a Post-Apocalyptic Wasteland where no women exsist. The human race cannot reproduce anymore and society has crashed. The absence of women also made all the men raging perverts who will do anything to just see a man dressed in a woman outfit. (Thats why the currency in this game is Porno Mags). The story follows Bradley Armstrong, a martial arts teacher who regrets his past. Years after this apocalypse Brad finds a newborn baby. A female newborn baby that can save humanity. Instead of using this baby to save humanity Brad keeps her and raises her as his own. Cut to many years later where the girl (who is called Buddy) is found and kidnapped. Your journey starts here.
GAMEPLAY:
Combat is done very well in this game. It is a turn based RPG where you can find and recruit many unique followers. All these followers have personality and their own special skills. You can change around your party to how you see fit and eventually you will discover a team combo that will win countless battles.
Be careful with your party members though. Many things in this game can perma kill your characthers, meaning theyre gone for good. Some events have a choice wether to sacrifice a team mate (killing him off for the rest of the game) or to have your own arm cutoff (that severly impacts Brad in combat). And if you dont like your teammates you can put em to the the test in Russian Roulette. If you win, you get Magezines! If you lose, eh. Some enemies have attacks that can perma death a party member. Youre not even safe when resting at campfires! Because resting in this wasteland can have a party member kiddnapped, your stuff taken or just some wierd thing like a man in a cave exploding on you. (THIS ACCTUALLY HAPPENS)
VISUALS/SOUND:
This games art reminds me of the Earthbound/Mother series (The humor does also, in a way). Every enemy and characther looks very well designed. Your party members also all have their unique animations also! And they all look great.
The sound design is also really great. Every song makes the mood of the situation amplify by 100. Some songs are really catchy and have a feel good mood to them. And some of the songs are absolutely terrifying. Just like the game.
OVERALL:
This game is an unforgettable experience that should be played if you want a good story, some laughs, some creepy moments, great combat and a kickass final battle.
9/10 (maybe a 10/10)
Sidenote: The sequel LISA: The Joyful is coming out this summer. Get ready.

Minecraft is a sandbox construction game created by Mojang AB founder Markus Persson, and inspired by the Infiniminer, Dwarf Fortress and Dungeon Keeper games. Gameplay involves players interacting with the game world by placing and breaking various types of blocks in a three-dimensional environment. In this environment, players can build creative structures, creations, and artwork on multiplayer servers and singleplayer worlds across multiple game modes.
Minecraft is available to all players for €19.95 (US$26.95, £17.32). When purchased, singleplayer and multiplayer game modes can be played using the downloadable stand-alone launcher. The official demo is free, but has a time limit. Minecraft development started around May 10, 2009, and pre-orders for the full game started being accepted on June 13, 2009. Minecraft's official release date was November 18, 2011. On September 20, 2014, Minecraft for the computer became the best-selling PC game of all time. On December 31, 2015, Minecraft for the computer reached 22 million sales.
On August 16, 2011, Minecraft: Pocket Edition was released for the Sony Xperia Play gaming smartphone. After its exclusivity with Sony expired, it was released for Android devices on October 7, 2011, and iOS devices on November 17, 2011 for US$6.99. On April 2, 2014, Minecraft was released for the Amazon Fire TV. It contains all the same features as the Pocket Edition as well as support for the Fire TV's controller. On December 10, 2014, Minecraft: Pocket Edition was released for Windows Phone 8.1. On January 10, 2015, Minecraft: Pocket Edition reached 30 million sales.
On May 9, 2012, Minecraft was released for the Xbox 360 on Xbox Live Arcade for US$20, where it subsequently broke every previous sales record.
On February 11, 2013, Minecraft: Pi Edition was released for the Raspberry Pi. The Pi Edition was intended as an educational tool for novice programmers and users are encouraged to open and change the game's code using its API. There were never any subsequent updates and the edition is now officially discontinued.
On December 17, 2013, Minecraft was released for the PlayStation 3 on the PlayStation Store for US$19.99. The release was almost identical to the Xbox 360 Edition and was developed in tandem with the Xbox 360 Edition from then on.
On June 26, 2014, the Xbox 360 & PlayStation 3 editions' sales passed the number of sales for the PC edition of Minecraft, leaving the Minecraft series having sold more than 72 million copies world-wide and becoming the third best-selling video game of all time.
Minecraft was released for the PlayStation 4 on September 4, 2014, the Xbox One on September 5, 2014 and the PlayStation Vita on October 14, 2014.
On September 15, 2014, Mojang AB and all of its assets (including Minecraft) were purchased by Microsoft for US$2.5 billion. On July 29, 2015, Minecraft was released for the universal Windows 10 platform as an adaptation of the Pocket Edition.
On December 17, 2015, the Wii U Edition was released.

Though the developer has said that Awkward Dimensions Redux is a collection of his dreams, in my experience it's more a collection of subconscious thoughts and feelings; maybe with a few dreams mixed in. The game is enjoyably bizarre and abstract, and it will most likely not appeal to analytical minds but rather those with a creative brain wave. There's a lot up for interpretation here, and much of the gameplay unfolds like an improvised interpretive dance.
The game is a collection of mini-levels, all with unique designs and mechanics. You'll never really understand what you're looking for, or what your goal is, that is until you find it. This may make it sound like Awkward Dimensions is frustrating, but it isn't; you'll end up stumbling into the answer very easily along the way. For instance, a personal favorite level of mine is Frame, where you're in an art gallery and you pick up a frame that shows you everything in black and white; all the while you're still able to see the colored world around you. The added catch is that the frame shows you rooms and objects that aren't visible with the naked eye, so you must use it to get to the next level.
In subject matter, this title deals with very personal feelings, but at the same time it's relatable to everyone since we've all experienced at least one of these emotions; fear of failure, the stress of college, a despairing break-up. However, a good core of the subject matter relates on an even deeper level with artists, and how we're basically faceless humans behind what we create, and that no one cares to look beyond the art form to see its creator; which is definitely something that I can relate to on a personal level. It also touches on coping with negative criticism, and there's an interesting FMV of the developer doing an on-stage performance piece about it.
Awkward Dimensions Redux lasts about an hour, and in that time it really makes you think; about life, lost love, your own fears, and that there are people behind the machine of art. Developers certainly are real people too, many subject to harsh criticism; some founded, some not so much. It's very easy to judge the creator, since we rarely get a glimpse of him, but it's even harder for someone who isn't creative at all to become a painter. Whether you realize it or not, artists in every form truly make the world go 'round, and that's what this game made me think about.

I guess I should give a FAIR review about this game.
So, let's talk about the Pros, Neutrals and Contras.
Pros:
-You can win any difficullty on any mission by yourself (you just need enough skill and the right equipment).
-You get rewarded if you search around on the whole map. You can collect probes which give you research points and with them you can unlock either better equipment (more-fueled jetpacks, extra ammo for a mech, etc) or new stuff for your weapons (♥♥♥♥ing laser sights, bigger magazines, etc) ---> Higher difficullty = more probes on a map.
-You get new stuff after getting a level-up. New weapons, new skins (armor, helmet and cape), etc...
-You progress on the galaxy-map with other players. 3 alien-races to fight against? Hell yea.
Neutral:
-The camera "forces" you to stick to each other. The enemies still spot you sometimes from a place you can't see because of the camera. At the same time it "forces" to play as an actual team and not everyone by himself.
Don't get me wrong, I like to play as a team! But sometimes I could just shoot into the camera instead of the enemy.
Cons:
-Even thou you and your team got good internet connection, the servers have their limits. I once shot someone in the back and there was blood coming out, but he didn't took any damage. Same goes with "walking someome over with a mech".
-The DLC's all togheter are like 50% of your arsenal.
-There is some equipment you will never or only rarely ever use. Included DLC-Stuff. Suggestion? Only buy a DLC if you REALLY want it.
-Some DLC's are not worth their price. Some weapons and equipment are unbalanced. In a bad way. (--> Some things need a buff in my eyes!)
-Many players use the laser-shotgun (for a reason). It counts as the "best" weapon out of all.
Personal opinion:
-You either play this game non-stop or just a few rounds each day/week. Sometimes you find trolls, but there is a report and like system.
"Report" = You don't actually "report" them, but you give this player a "dislike" which means this player will more likely be put with other "trolls" when looking for a game in the multiplayer-list or waiting for player support after calling a beacon inside of a mission. And... "Like"...well, it does the opposite, duh.
-I don't get the 3 free expansions you get when buying the standard game. xD (You can see them in the game main menu at the bottom right. I guess we will find out when the time comes or I'm just to stupid to get it..)
I guess that's about it. Hope you found my review helpful and we might see each other in the next game!
...And sorry for such a long review. :P

Now, whilst I agree, grinds are never usually very fun at all, 30 hours, even 10 hours for £16... I think this is a bargain. You'll be spending, what is it these days? £40? £50 on new AAA games that give, usually, a max of 30 hours gameplay. That is more than double the price... DOUBLE. Wow.
Another comparison comes to mind... Where I live, you'll pay around £14 to go to the cinema and see a movie, plus popcorn, drinks, what ever else. Now just have a quick Google on how long the 'longest film' is...
Alright, I wasn't prepared for what I just asked you to Google... apparantly the longest film is over 850 hours... My point is that most films are 2 hours long! So we come back to the whole comparison of money exchanged for 'time entertained', and again this is a bargain!
There was also a complaint about some 'snow boots' or something being locked behind a paywall. That it stops you experiencing the game properly or some♥♥♥♥♥♥ Basically, I'm calling bull on that. Whoever complained at this, saw someone else with that perk and felt but-hurt when they had to pay for it. The snow areas are there to add MORE of a challenge to the already brutal game, but you can pay if you don't want to experience the game that way. (translation: if you don't want to experience the game the way it was designed originally...)

This game relies heavily on Alexander Pushkin's 1833 short story
which is a story well known to every Russian, and at least heard of by many in western Europe, though it seems to be recognized by only a few in the Americas, both North and South. It will help your enjoyment of this visual novel to at the very least read a synopsis or overview such as this one at Wikipedia:
. The game will be even more enjoyable if you read or listen to the short story, and links to both print and audio versions (English translations) are located at the bottom of the Wikipedia page accessible through the link above.
The game seems to be targeted at an adolescent audience, roughly from age 9 to 16, though this will vary depending on cultural and sub-cultural norms. The game's story line has some sexual allusions, which are no worse than anything you'll find in standard fare on tele in western nations, you'll find much more directly explicit content at cinema almost any day.
Youth and adults from 17 on up probably won't find much entertainment value in this game unless, like me, you're entertained by direct observational learning. In that regard there is much to be gained from researching surrounding topics (such as the story
and its place in Russian culture and literature as well as Pushkin's place in the pantheon of great Russian writers whose influence was and still is felt around the world, and Russian culture, in particular a portion of which isn't often looked at by those of us in the west -- that of Russian adolescence, and how strikingly similar it is to all other cultures in many ways, while in other ways being different). If topics like that don't interest you, and you don't like asking "why" or “how”, and then spending time (sometimes lots of it) researching the answer, then this visual novel has nothing for you and you will end up falling in line with many of the negative reviewers. In those cases don't waste your time with it. If you are younger and have little or no experience with Russian, ethnically German Russian, or formerly Soviet cultures, then this visual novel will not be fun for you. If you are of the age group, and are from or at least very familiar with the above mentioned cultures as they exist today, you will be able to relate to these characters and the story, and may find it a fun read.

The story is very short, and I probably would have finished it in under an hour and a half if it were not for a forty-five minute interruption in the middle of it for which I did not have the time to save and exit.

And then there's the ones that everyone complains of: A fairly large amount of cash for the commanders, which basically dictate your playstyle. So if you want to use the flavor-of-the-month "OP" commanders for that given week or whatever, or even if you want to play the game a different way, (especially considering some of these "perks" I mentioned earlier require some of the units you can only get by using these premium commanders) you either need to stump up the green and pay the piper, or you have to grind for days (And I mean days, it IS an RTS after all) for the in-game currency. And that trickles in at, from what I know, 500 per level-up. That's not much, considering you need like 25k at least or so to get these commanders. But again, you COULD just dump real money into them. Which gives you the same thing as if you had ground for days. This keeps coming up in my games and it's disappointing, it just makes taking time to get to know the game's ins-and-outs worthless. Why try when you can just pay for everything? Oh right, because you could buy an entire 'nother game with that money.
Speaking of which... yeah, I can't in good conscience say this is a good buy. ♥♥♥♥ing... ten bucks or so for a Sturmtiger. That's just baiting.
Edit: For the record, I looked up a forum thread or two on "Warspoils Farming", or farming the system that gives you your after-game drops. What I found was... hilarious. Okay, so I started playing this game about two years ago and only made it to the second location because the game is buggy as Hell and wasn't loading something that was an intergral part of one of my missions (so, I quit instead of starting over).
I recently replayed the game, all the way through, this time, and let me tell you: this game is fantastic.
I's an old game, sure, but it definitely holds up well. And in some ways, is vastly superior to some modern games. The graphics are a bit dated, but not horribly so. Again, I've played some modern games with worse. Voice acting is top-notch. The story and lore that surrounds the game is amazing and deep. You could spend hours just talking to NPCs because the lore is that involved and you may want to absorb it all. I hesitate to say characters are believable (I'm looking at you, Knox), but they're charming. Some are likeable, whereas others are easy to hate. Either way, they're all written well for the world they are in and really help to develop it. I found the Anarchs to be a much more relatable, realistic group than some of the others. That said, the members of the Anarchs are my favorite chraracters, so I could be biased.
Combat (especially melee) can be a bit clunky, but not impossible to handle. And, due to the various clans, it makes it very easy to find a playstyle that works best with what you like. This game transitions from a stealth/puzzle game, to a 3rd person hack and slash, to a 1st person shooter seamlessly, and allows the player to change up their playstyle on the fly.
Each clan has a very unique, rich story that surrounds them, which makes it fun to play multiple times in order to get a feel for all seven of them.
Some the levels are unsettling, or downright scary to go through. They're very atmospheric, with great audio and visuals. I would be lying if I said that there weren't some missions where I had to take my headphones off, or had to play during daylight hours while other people were around. There's one in particular where you don't even face any enemies, but the hair on the back of my neck still stands up every time I go through it.
My one main complaint is that VTMB is a game that hinges on the fact that your character might be a sexual creature, making it possible to sort of romance some of the characters. However, there is only one male NPC throughout the game who can be 'romanced', yet several females. I get that at the time, game companies thought  that female gamers were a rarety, so I don't really fault it too much.

A cute little visual novel about the struggles of a would-be professional calligrapher. A very simple story, but still touching, as it deals with the kinds of problems and frustrations that we all have to deal with as we grow up and try to find our place in the world. The few choices are fairly cut-and-dry: each time, one option continues the story, while the other goes to a bad end. It's fairly obvious which option is the better one. They do help emulate the little decisions we make each day that compund to affect our lives in a more profound manner later.
The art is decent, if nothing special. The character art is charming, in a chibi style that helps counterbalance the more serious subject matter. The background art paints a decent picture, but isn't really memorable. The few tracks of the music work well with the subject matter and art, helping to set the tone of the story.
The story itself is very short (20-25 minutes or so to go through all the paths), but since it's a free game made by a very small team that isn't a criticism, as the game is good for what it is: a quick dive into the life of another person. If you want a quick VN fix, it's worth it to give this one a try.

Playing this game is like loosing your Soul in space.
For $3, a no-brainer buy, provided you're into indie space-based roguelike-like games.

The good: Random, roguelike play, text based rpg aspects, no two games are alike. Unlocks, and varations on how you set up your ships (I don't mean the layouts but after you start) lead to much replayability.
The bad: The game does everything it can to make you miserable and or lose. Before the expansion this was also true but not quite so vehemently. The end boss even on easy is impossible for me but apparently some people have solved it. After 64 hours I am giving up on it. Even with Advanced mode off the game is 10x harder than it was. Getting near my scores of several years ago is severely challenging in a bad way. Sometimes it feels like a run through is a complete waste of time.
The ugly: What do you want for cheap? The game is too hard for people who aren't willing to dedicate their lives to solving it. I suspect being under 40 years old helps (because lets face it us old folks just aren't as 'smart' as we used to be.) And having the patience of job probably doesn't hurt either. The game has no frills graphics which I like but may be unexciting for those raised on MMOs and fancy gizmos.
Overall: There is plenty of fun in it and I would recommend it for anyone who doesn't mind losing. All the time. Where you lose in the game will vary and much of the time it won't seem like you have much control over it. Even if you are great at multitasking and micromanaging the challenges are insurmountable. This is the nature of Rogue's descendents. Even those set in space. Except for the ones that are more 'like-lite' than 'like'.
As they say the meaning is in the journey not in the destination so play it and revel in the many fiery deaths you get to experience.
Unlocking ships is a mini game that can be fun if you get very lucky. I've managed 4 in 4 years so hey. Advanced edition offers more things to confound, amuse and mystify you. (New races, items, ships, etc)
Don't be embarrassed to play on easy and don't forget to look for help because the game is designed to be ultra hard even on the easy mode. (There are people who will need to show their epine by claiming otherwise but ignore them. The truth is you learn in baby steps and die repeatedly, horribly and without mercy. You do get to do pretty mean things to others while doing so, so there is that.)
Especially learn what the basics of the game are and then learn the basic 'no nos' because that will get you pretty far. Sector 8 is not hard to get to (though intact may be a different story) once you've managed to get to sector 5 which is not hard to get to once you learn how to get through sectors without being blown randomly. And then you get to learn how to die to the Rebel Flagship. If not in the first battle then in the next or the last. Only the lucky and skillful survive the final battle. I am neither so far.

I have not in a long time played such a roguelike that captures all the difficulty and strategy of Shiren the Wanderer style games, and successfully marries it with unique quirks of its own. This title is one that I can say really brings a completely new feel to the roguelike genre.
More in line with newer roguelikes, it is an easy to pick up, hard to master game with the freedom to tackle it how you please. The side-scrolling aspect of it keeps you on your toes and constantly vigilant. You're forced to move a quick pace to outrun the darkness, but are still given the ability to search for loot at as much leisure that can be allowed. In a way, this really brings the right level of tension and speed to the game. Not to mention the music. It really caught me off guard and I found myself humming many of the songs.
In summation, if you're looking for a new game to add to your collection this should be a prime candidate. The playthroughs are quick, but extremely fun. At three dollars, saying this is a steal is an understatement.

+Heavily inspired by Earthbound
+Large cast of characters to customize your battle tactics
+Dark dystopian world, adult storyline, a lot of adult humor
+Interesting combat system that uses key/button presses to create combos
+Encourages item usage versus hording
+Have to make tough choices - lose your best ally or your arm?
-World layout can be confusing; it's easy to forget where something or someone was
+/-High difficulty early on due to no random encounters, limited ability to earn "mags" (currency)
This game is Overwhelming Positive for a reason.  Worth every dollar.

Okay, so, I'm not one to tell a person that their art is "good" or "bad" or whatever, because that is not my place to say. Art is subjective and this game feels like it's meant to be judged as a piece of art. However, being critical about it is perfectly acceptable, so, if somehow the developer reads this, I just want them to know that, so they don't feel disheartened. Just getting that out the way.
Firstly, the game is free, so, nothing gained, nothing lost (except perhaps time). If this game was even £1 however, I would feel incredibly cheated, especially considering free games like Spooky's House Of Jump Scares gave me much more from my expectations. Despite a multitude of levels, I don't feel as if I had been engaged in any way. While I persume these to be interpretations of dreams or something (going from the "About this game" segment), they just felt meaningless. Which, granted, to the dreamer or the dev or whoever, they may mean something, but as a player going through these, I could only really relate to one, which was the level about getting over this girl and everything was grey except for an omnispresent text block in the sky. I understand there was some developers commentary which may have possibly aided in this issue (I didn't listen to it), but, as a player, we just want to get into the game, so why that commentary or narration was not included in the main game, I don't quite know.
Secondly, and for me personally, the most damning, this just felt like it was blatantly ripping off The Beginner's Guide, which is probably one of my most favourite games and one I find I can always go back to. At one point (and I don't know if this particular piece of music I'm referring to is copyrighted or not) I swear I could hear a song that was from one of the levels from The Beginner's Guide. I could have been mistaken but, even so, the choice to use even a similar piece and have that link being made is enough to cause unhappiness. Especially as I was travelling up a ladder at the same speed as a turtle on land while watching some weird performance of a dude throwing paper in the air.
My last critique that I can be arsed to write is that the game overall just felt rushed. If this was a man or woman's dreams and thoughts and feelings put into a game, it felt as if they didn't really care too much for it. I understand that money and time, etc. may get in the way of creating a truly polished game, however, I feel that this had so much potential that was just... wasted.
So, even though this is free, I wouldn't recommend this game, and this is coming from a guy who loves indie games that have some emotion, heart and soul in them. Perhaps if more time went into tweaking levels, making them more polished and in some cases just fixing them (some levels just didn't want to work because falling) then this game COULD be good, but, it would take a lot in my opinion. But, the potential is there.

TLDR: A very fun game for a short time which afterwards to boils down to a pointless grind. Some of the DLC seems like it should be a feature in-game, with some way to unlock. The playerbase is great, but small, which prevents you from trying some of the more challenging gamemodes (unless you have 3 other friends who play the game as well.) Difficulty is binary.
Majority of the things that should be features, example: All Terrain Boots aka AT Boots, are locked behind a DLC paywall. There are few much less effective alternatives to this, but unlocking any of them is a pain. AT Boots is the only true remover of the Snow planet debuff which slows your character and prevents them from sprinting (in a game thats all about moving fast and killing faster).
The playerbase, while helpful and non-toxic, just doesn't seem to be big enough, as more challenging missions require more players for pure firepower in different direction, and there is very few playing above or at the 6 - Very Challenging Difficulty (it goes up to 12). Much could be improved with matchmaking (although the problem may stem from the seemingly low playerbase.
Diffculty in this game is also binary: Either you have the firepower and equipment to take out the hordes of enemies, or you are simply numbered. If you are outnumbed, this results in an 8 minute circle of 3 out of the 4 squad members dieing, one reviving them all, and all but 1 dieing again. Otherwise, in singleplayers, it is just dying twice and failing or aborting the mission.

This game is plain dumb and fun and I love it. Game's only got 4 notable problems IMO.
It's a good game aside from the below problems. Looks like a mindless twinstick shooter, but actually has loads of coordination! Heck, you can even coordinate with other players as you construct your builds before actually starting the missions. Pretty awesome.
I'm not going to be writing this review to try to sell you the game though, I'm just writing it so you'll be aware of certain things I don't like about the game if you plan on buying it.
There are 3 races in the game: Cyborgs, Bugs, and Illuminates. Throughout all the planets you fight on in this game, you will fight against one of these races at a time. The Cyborgs and Bugs are actually very fun to fight, while the Illuminates are not.
On lower difficulties, only the weakest Illuminate enemies spawn, making them the easiest to fight. On high difficulties, Illuminates spawn in large quantities, often on top of you, or if you're trying to reinforce dead teammates, ontop of their pods when they drop in. If the Illuminates enemies aren't close by, it's often because they are Obelisks or enemies with laser-sniping abilities.
Now, let's say you're playing a higher difficulty where all types of Illuminates spawn in. All of the special types that start spawning have
attacks that feel plain unfair.
Illusionists fire projectiles that invert your controls, which are difficult to avoid because such projectiles explode (and any players caught in the explosion will be affected).
Council Members fire projectiles similar to those of Illusionists, except they
, and they also home in. They also fire out a wave that inverts your controls if you're close enough, and it doesn't matter how big the wave seems at the time, anybody in the maximum radius of the wave is affected, instantly. The Council Members can also attack even if you stagger them. Very annoying.
The scouts sound the alarm so quickly you need a gun that one-shots them to deal with them effectively.
The laser snipers (don't know their actual name, and don't care) always are offscreen and annoyingly snipe your objectives.
The Tripods always spawn in large numbers and stay ontop of you or your pods when you try to reinforce people.
The Obelisks fire walls that instantly kill you, some utility strategems (mechs, tanks, etc.), and some objects, and make it so jetpacks are required since the walls block players.
Illuminates are annoying and are not fun to fight.
I mentioned Illuminates being annoying. Now, think about how I said Cyborgs and Bugs are fun to play. Now, imagine only being able to play on Illuminate missions. This happens sometimes because people hate playing Illuminate missions and love playing Cyborg/Bug missions.
Every mission you complete in a sector of planets grants that sector influence points. When enough of these are attained, the sector is locked off and you continue to the next. When all sectors for a particular race are cleared, that race is out of the war and you need to wait for the war to end and for all sectors to reset to be able to play missions with that race again.
It wouldn't be so bad if all the races were fun to play with, and it especially wouldn't be so bad if often you weren't restricted to Homeworld Assaults (which are the last things done for each race). During Homeworld Assaults, you can't unlock items at all (unless they are level-locked items). Thankfully, only non-DLC items need to be unlocked, but this is still super annoying since you really do need many of the non-DLC items to play effectively.
I like the music in this game, good work to whoever made it! Only problem is, the music that plays during a mission depends solely on the race and difficulty you're playing on. If you keep doing Cyborg missions of difficulty 9 or higher, you will always hear the same theme. Minorly annoying, but hey, the music for the high difficulty Cyborg missions is awesome. I just don't like hearing it 50 billion times.
Think of an exponential curve. It starts out super shallow, not increasing rapidly, and then over time the speed at which it increases skyrockets. That's this game's difficulty curve. Difficulties 1-8 are pretty easy once you get used to the game, and difficulty 9 is the "I need to start paying attention" difficulty. Difficulties beyond that (10-12) can actually be pretty challenging.
Most of what I have to say is negative, but that's only because I wanted to point out the flaws with this game. It's pretty good, but it's not perfect. The flaws aren't so bad that I wouldn't recommend the game. It's a solid game with fun gameplay for the most part.

I can't recommend this game. It plays quite well actually and the base way that it all works together is really great. Buildings can fall. Things can be set on fire. It's really damn good in that regard. Again, the base aspects and mechanics are great and a lot of you will find this game to be really good.
Because of the net code and community I just can't recommend it.
Originally I hadn't enjoyed the game, then I played on a couple of modded servers and the modded servers are pretty great, but the net code for this game and how it all functions makes it wonky at times especially when a lot is going on. I don't really like how you can walk through a door, then back through it, wait a few seconds and then die all with 80 or less ping. Inversely you could swing your sword twice and think you missed and then the archer 10 feet away from you dies and you get the kill, again with 80 or less ping.
I just don't feel that I really had fun with the time spent.
I WOULD have recommended getting it just to play on the modded servers, but I found that a lot of the communities in them are...immature. I originally praised a lot of the servers for being really unique and fun, but lo and behold after playing them for a while it starts to become apparent that no one is really 'older' in their mind sets. On a zombie survival server we were playing as normal, shooting ballista/crossbow turrets when all of a sudden someone spawns in and starts yelling random crap about us needing to get off the turrets. He gets mad because we won't and starts griefing. No one would vote kick him until it was too late. Game ruined.
This happens everywhere and while most of the admins for the servers tend to be right minded, it seems like none of them are on on any of the servers when I'm around. I'm assuming the game is more appealing in the UK since if I get on really early in the moring (EST) I see a lot of people on and everyone's cheerful. Get on late at night and everyone's childish and just generally sucks.
This goes doubly for servers like Aphelion's roleplay where there is pretty much no admins on when I'm around, but someone is always griefing or not playing by the rules. I can't really recommend that server either in spite of how awesome it's design and mechanics are because the guy who was modding it left to go make his own game and doesn't take care of anyone who donates anymore. I respect the desire to move onto another game, but not to leave what you've created behind while still promising things that you can't deliver for monetary gain.
Again, with all this in mind and just how the game plays and how much it's priced, I just can't recommend it. For a game that heavily requires other players you really have to like the base game a lot to ignore the community. And if you're on when most of the population and cool guys are on, good for you and I hope you have fun. For someone like myself though I guess I was just fooling myself into believeing that I could find a modded server community that was good enough to make the game up to the standards I'd held it to initially.
TL:DR - String of bad experiences with community and not a fan of net code. Don't think it's worth the base cost.

This is a kinetic novel about girls who tell campy horror stories to each other one night. Kinetic novel means no choices, so you can just click and read at your own pace.
The whole story is just about one hour read so I won't get into details. The stories are fun and scary, all situated at (summer) camps. The translation is pretty good and I noticed only a couple of typos (in the English script) along the way, so it shouldn't be too annoying for most people. There's also a Russian version.
Since it's free, complaining is not very fair but I'm going to do it anyway. Sometimes it was a bit confusing to see who was talking, especially in the beginning when you don't really know every character yet and then four, or five or even six of them are in the scene talking together.
Also, I played the game through on a laptop. For some reason the game got the laptop really hot and it burned through my battery really fast, showing 30 min left at 50% mark, when usually this would still last me 2.5 hours. So the game engine (built on Unity) could probably use some optimization (I used "fastest" settings). Not that most people would notice this though, playing on PCs or laptops hooked to a wall, so this is a rather minor qualm.
You might notice that the characters are almost the same as in Everlasting Summer. They have the same character artist, though different teams made them.
There's a couple of flashy cutscenes and generally the visuals are nice. Overall, it's a quite good for a short visual novel, and you really can't argue much against that price point.

This game is hella great but you know whats better? This outstanding pie recipe.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

This game is fun for a few hours, but it loses it's appeal once you've played all the mission types.  The game universe resets every 20-30 days so that you can once again win the war for Super Earth, which is nice so that you can continue playing the game but also very annoying since you have to watch the War Victory cut scene every few weeks.
You can play missions in three sectors of the galaxy.  Each sector is controlled by a different alien race.  The races have slightly different strengths and weaknesses, but are overall pretty similar.  The planets have slightly varied environments, but you do end up seeing the same level design over and over again.  The selection of mission objectives are not very diverse and include bomb sweeping, pick up and deliver, defend a location, destroy a location, or activate some equipment.
Repeatedly playing the game will earn you experience, and each level has a number of collectibles you can pick up to unlock research points.  Experience and research points grant you new gear or upgrade existing gear.  I found that the gear unlocked by level 5 or so was pretty much the best gear to use for my play style, so all future experience and research points just went unspent.  The vast majority of weapons and special abilities are garbage, so there's simply no appeal to keep playing and try to unlock better equipment.
Missions have varying difficulty levels which are adjusted not by the objectives you have to perform but rather by the enemies you have to face.  There are more enemies, and they are more difficult enemies, in the higher difficulty levels.  Since it doesn't take special gear to defeat those enemies, a low level player can be just as successful in those harder levels as a player with hundreds of hours.  This ultimately means you'll be able to experience everything the game has to offer in only a few hours of playtime without actually having to build up to anything.
Ultimately this game is a highly repetitive grind simply for the sake of grinding.  It grows boring quickly regardless of if you play solo, with friends, or with random people online.  I found myself wishing for an end-game of some type at the 10-hour point, but Helldivers simply doesn't have one to offer.

As true a diamond in the rough as any game you can find here. Well, well worth the time of anyone who's interested in RPGs, arcane / urban / supernatural horror atmosphere, good writing in games or good plotting in gaming. If this is on sale you're cheating yourself if you don't give it a go.
The premise in a nutshell: Your character goes on a bender and ends up dead, then undead. Saved from certain (final) death, you end up an investigator / fixer for a secret shadow society of urbane monsters, chasing down all sorts of weird happenings in and around nighttime Los Angeles. Talk, fight, and use your monstrous powers to manipulate or destroy hapless mortals and other, less redeemable things.
Let's start with the good: The plotting, writing, atmosphere are all simply amazing. From the marketing materials and screenshots you might assume the game is grim and gritty and oh-so-goth, but the game is, for the most part, incredibly funny. Think Deadpool or Garth Ennis' comics - there's a lot of black humor. Most everybody is dead and loving it. And it's not possible to say enough about how incredible the voice talent cast is, with a small handful of exceptions. Yes, that's Bender showing you the vampiric ropes in the tutorial. If the premise seems ridiculous at first, the game will sell  you on it. The central mystery is really good and the sense of dread builds perfectly.
The atmosphere of the game is great - much like Deus Ex, it makes the most of being set entirely at night. There is a definite sense of traversing the city of angels' seedy underbelly - while the rest of the world's sleeping, all the weirdos and club kids and dirty cops and streetwalkers come out to play. If you look hard enough you'll find not just other vampires but stranger, more sinister, and inexplicable things preying on humans. the original soundtrack is very good and mostly trip-hop influencedm and the licensed soundtrack (mostly playing in clubs) is, well... It's subpar goth metal, for the most part, but all the files are in .mp3 format so you can switch them out for whatever you want.*
The narrative is composed of several story strands and subplots but is structured in "hubs and spokes" - think Hell's Kitchen in Deus Ex or Omega Station in Mass Effect 2. Each city center (there are four) is a large street-level area, thick with opportunities to take on new quests, pick fights, steal money or blood.
As with any classic RPG, you have stats, skills and powers that you level up (note that experience is given on quest completion, not upon killing♥♥♥♥♥♥- it's just as viable, and probably more fun, to play a stealthy character). There are no classes but you do choose a "clan", sort of a vampiric race. One thing you'll constantly hear people rave about with this game is how different the game can get based on this choice - most are interchangeable (save for the powers given clans are allowed) but the Malkavians are marked by insanity, and so every single line of dialogue you can give in the game is rewritten as a bizarre riddle (it's fun to talk to NPCs as they try to make sense of you). Nosferatu, on the other hand, are clearly monstrous, and so most every human you interact with will freak out, if they assume you're not a burn victim or wearing a costume.
Fighting gameplay is fairly good, though hardly exceptional. This came out before the advent of cover-based shooting so it may take some getting used to. Guns kind of suck unless you really know what you're doing. Melee can be fun but can also drag. Using your powers is always fun, you just have to watch your blood level (basically mana) - invest in the "brawling skill" so that you drain enemy blood in the middle of combat. Sneaking is pretty satisfying and intuitive.
The visuals are pretty fugly, and the animations in gameplay are bit janky, with the very notable exception of the dialogue animations - Troika took full advantage of the rigging potential of the then-young Source Engine (V:tmB rather infamously released on the same day as Half-Life 2, to its detriment) and as a result the conversations hold up to this day- it's crazy to go from this to, say, Mass Effect and marvel how much more expressive NPCs are here.
Bloodlines has its warts - Chinatown is full of caricatures, the lack of polish over the whole product is stupendously evident and a community patch is more or less essential to play the game to its fullest - but believe me when I tell you that there is no other game like this. When it gets its hooks in you, you'll play it to the end, and when it's over you'll wish you could spend more time exploring its strange, sinister world.

Fan of RPG and having played the first one, I had to at least play the sequel. The sequel will differ dramatically from the first game in the following ways:
1) You get party members early in the game that you can keep (last game gave you party members near the end of the game)
2) Everything is dark + bleak to set the story's setting (which I think makes sense for the story plot, but for the player, the very dimmed gameplay just makes it irritating to play - note: later in review I elaborate)
3) You don't start off very weak (you aren't at level 1 so you don't have to grind as hard to reach max lvl - 60).
4) Slightly more story plot in the sequel than the first (this will only apply if you played the first and then play this, but then again, why would you play the sequel only...)
I liked the changes in the sequel, but the dimmed setting can irritate a player. The story's setting has the world of labyronia plunged into a forever winter where monsters run rampant. While the dimmed lighting, purposely darkened screens, and darkened setting serve a purpose in setting the plot, it annoyed me as it was very difficult to distinguish on-screen graphics. Because everything was dark or a shade of black, it is hard to tell if that is a space you can/not walk on in Carralan - irritated me since I had to kept walking back and forth to figure out where I was suppose to go at the beginning. Other times, you just miss things all together because everything looks black-ish, or you are forced to keep walking around in a trial+error fashion. IE: labyrinth mazes are pretty much annoying because you seriously can't see much until you explore + remember the whole place.
Another change in the game is the 'cues'. It used to be you learn skill(s) from finding 'cues' but this sequel has removed almost 99% of the skills learned from 'cues'. Ann, to my knowledge, is the only one that still learns skills via interaction with objects. Everyone else learns via leveling or finding/buying manuals. I liked the aspect of finding cues and I do miss this aspect of the game. Truth be told, slightly disappointed that there wasn't a final skill to be learned when you max out the character's level. :(
I notice some imbalance of exp + gold per monster. The difficulty ratings of a monster should be correlated to the amount of exp and gold reaped when you slay it. Some monsters do not follow this very well and it can be a very tough time at the beginning of the game where you need some gold to progress + survive better.
Improvements from last game:
In the first game, there were large stages where you can easily get lost, because the map loops itself. In this sequel, there aren't as many overly large maps that you can wander lost forever now. The stages are still large, but most of them are more constricted. Although, the last section of the game's map was very annoying. I think the next part of the game (Labyronia 3?) will benefit the most if they remove the last bits of maps that are like this.
The graphics are similar, but monster sprites look better now. They aren't as pixelated. However, I noticed that in the armagen battles, the battle scenes are delayed or the monster stops attacking me for no reason. Especially in the final boss battle, I entered all the battle commands (IE: defend/attack/etc), but there is a delay before the characters act them out.
In the first game, you can get lost as to what to do first, but this game has improved on it where it's mostly linear and it should be clear as to where you are progressing... until you get the airship, which it's up to you to remember where you are in the game. However, it should be clear still and it is a definite improvement from the first.
The puzzle aspects of this game are definitely better than the first. It took me awhile to figure out the Hallway of Mirrors and the side quests inserted into the game made it more amusing to play. The puzzles were largely not hard and just makes you feel good about yourself since you can solve them after a little thought.
"Hidden secrets" in the game. There are just a few of these that I found and those mentioned from others in the discussion page. I wished there was a bit more in developing this area, because everytime I play an RPG and I get free-range of travel (airship/teleportation), my first thought is to travel and find secrets. If you played the first part of this game, then you will mostly know where you want to go to check. Otherwise, you will need to follow a guide to look for some. Although, the current guides don't cover them 100%.
Overall, the game is enjoyable and has improved since it's first one, I didn't get as frustrated until I reached stages of the game where shadows and dimmed parts are inserted (aggravation). If there is going to be a labyronia 3, I look forward to trying it and hopefully it keeps all the good parts from Labyronia 1+2 and none of the bad. 8/10!

A brief warning: I realize this review is going to sound quite harsh, and normally I do try to be lenient when writing reviews, but this is a case where brutal honesty is the only real possible option.   Saying that, this game had great potential, but unfortunately, it wasn't executed all that well.  To start with, there is absolutely no correlation between the beginning of the game and the end.  There's a kind of a little prolog at the very start that then transitions into the main story, but it doesn't come up in the game again.  However there is a very vague referencing to it towards the end of the game, but that's it.  Also, the ending was extremely anticlimactic.  The way the game progressed was rather good and there was enough build-up that I was excited to see the "main event" of the game, which was mentioned by the characters in the beginning... but then the story just completely flops, like the developer ran out of time to do a proper ending and just slapped something in to call it finished.
Now, within the game, there are mini stories
.  These stories were done well enough, but they seemed half-hearted.  The whole time these stories are being told all you see is the character doing the storytelling.  There is an occasional image related to the story being told to break up the monotony, but otherwise, it's completely disengaging.  When I play a game, even a visual novel, I want to get pulled into the story.  This game just didn't have that.  The mini stories needed to be more fleshed out, such as adding visuals to the narration or even a change in the background, just something!  Not just one of the characters switching poses occasionally, which was actually a little distracting in my opinion.
Now, my chief complaint about this game is the characters.  It was difficult to tell who was talking at some points because there is really no chance to learn who is who, thus making it a headache to match the sea of names to the characters on screen.  It was irritating, but not so disorientating that it became a huge problem.  The most distracting thing was the characters themselves.  The art style is nice, I have no complaints about that, it was the poses of the characters that really threw me off.  They just didn't make sense half the time, which broke my focus from the game to ponder why the developer chose to a) include the pose to begin with and b) use it in situations where it didn't belong.  Not to mention the needless sexualization at some parts.  I'm guessing the characters are all somewhere in their teenage years (minus one obvious one), so some sexuality is generally expected... but it seemed to just be thrown in randomly, yet again distracting from the game and making me wonder why?
I know the game is free, so I guess I should give it some slack.  All in all, it wasn't all that bad, but the parts that were just stuck out like a sore thumb.  I honestly do think the game had potential and that the developer simply ran out of time making it or something, because it was just too disjointed for that not to be the case.  I would love to see a revamp where more time and care was put into it.  And I don't mean to rag on the developer so much.  The game just seemed so carelessly thrown together, and I'm just really disappointed because I think this game could have been really good.

First things first, do you like Roguelikes? If so then this game is a very prospective find for your collection! It's a very perma death and turn based unforgiving type game but of course it has features that work around that kind of system, being able to bring items over from previous gameplays and also unlocking new classes and perks to make yourself stronger at the beginning. The pace it sets with the darkness constantly chasing you is very fresh as well because not only is it a roguelike game but it also has aspects of time management almost like Half Minute Hero, making gameplay have a much more frantic pace even though it's still turn based. Another thing that makes the game fun to play is the online features, it's always fun playing a game and knowing others are doing the same, the little pop in messages aren't disruptive at all and seeing how far other people are reaching and how many other people are failing is fun in it's own rights. Of course, it's got the sharing aspect from games like Minecraft and Starbound, you can share any of the worlds that have been generated by simply giving the world's code to friends and other people. All the worlds have their own little leaderboards too, with rankings and other things, you can even see how people went about their adventure. Also, you can actually get better at a world/dimension since it's layout never changes aside from random loot drops and events. Overall, while simplistic and a bit more on the hectic/rushed side, it's still pretty in depth, especially with the carryovers and whatnot, you can even grind items out to twink yourself up for the next run. As an ending note, don't expect to win early on unless you play on the easiest difficulty, losses are inevitable on this game as they are a part of it, take it in as it comes and build yourself up to become stronger to finally defeat the Demon Lord!

I was new to the Metro series, having not played the originals (but being aware of them) due to putting my time into other games. However, I picked up 2033 and Last Light for under $10 in a sale last year, because it seemed like a good deal, and I needed to get away from the mind-racking strategy games that had been dominating my gaming experience lately. I was not disappointed by Metro 2033 Redux, at all!
I'm usually a fiend for open-world style games, but the linerar progression in Metro 2033 didn't bother me in the slightest, and integrates your character into a well-told and immersive story about as well as you could hope from a game. A good variety of interesting and, at times, original, weapons; a good balance of human and non-human enemies; none of the achievements were outlandishly ridiculous to accomplish; and the atmosphere was dark and dreary, but also believable and authentic.
After playing through the game twice this month (Nov.'17), once focusing more on assault, the second focusing more on stealth, I can't wait to continue the series with Metro Last Light.

Aesthetically speaking it's excellent, this is a good looking game and I love the period it's set in, the cars and the music all fantastic. The weapons have real bite, the cars have real weight and the voice acting has conviction. But this game is filled with litle niggles which on their own wouldn't bother me, but there are so many of them that it really bogs down the experience. The sparsity of checkpoints is easily the worst problem, the number of times i've been killed while behind solid cover is a joke and the car controls are far too twitchy, making a complete mockery of the game's fantastic physics model. What I really hate is that pretty much all of these problems feel like they could of been ironed out with a little more work from the developers, this is by no means a bad game but it doesn't feel like a polished product.

I wish there was a neutral option. Although it's a good game, Labyronia 2 feels like it has taken several steps back, in comparison with the original. Most of the stuff that I disliked were new features and story direction that the creators were trying out. It's clear that they're attempting to improve the entire structure of their series, and kudos for them, but it just didn't work out.
The cons:
- Travel is much more linear than it predecessor. (In the first game, you could go to about a dozen different areas from the very beginning. In this game, you're limited to only 1-2 new places to visit at any given point of the story)
- Some labyrinths were pretty straightforward.
- Certain battle functions aren't coherent and bug out sometimes (Mainly AoE attacks, especially Garic's).
- Plot is short. Dialogues are long. Tends to be boring and time consuming unnecessarily (Especially before difficult boss fights that you die through a few times. )
- Most "puzzles" weren't even puzzles. You just had to move boulders around, light stuff on fire, and that's about it.
The pros:
+ Challenging from the start.
+ You get more party members early on.
+ Battles are more strategic. Even random encounters require fighting strategically if you wish to survive.
+ Some labyrinths had interesting obstacles to overcome.
+ Main characters have some decent writing.

****  4 out of 5 stars in my opinion.
Yes, I really enjoyed playing this game. Graphics, for 2009, are quite good, explosions are well done, and it is played in real-time. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is smart, but can be overcome as it tends to repeat most of its moves at each mission restart (predictability). But, you will be CHALLENGED to get through some of the missions and strategy will be required as the enemy will change its strategy in ways that you may not expect. The AI will provide some "surprises" which makes it entertaining. It will keep you alert (situation awareness) and busy planning your strategy. I found it to be quite ENGAGING and felt determined to finish it - and did. It has been 5 years since I played it, but I remember it as one of my favorites in this genre. Try the DEMO and decide.

It isn't for everyone, and the difficulty and learning curve are both high. It's commonly compared to Company of heroes. Men of War has more functionality but less polish. You can do more things, for example, steal enemy vehicles and weapons, and with the line of sight, stealth is sometimes a viable option. I'd reccommend it if you like Company of Heroes and are looking for a more indepth experience. The campaign is great once you understand how to play. For Multiplayer, you might want to try Men of war : Assault Squad.

So, I neglected playing this title for quite some time.  I finally got around to reading it.  Finally, my review has come in.
is a FREE kinetic visual novel about a few teens and a loli telling campfire stories indoors to pass the time.  Instead of it being scary or terrifying as you might expect from the game's description and trailer, it's more tame than you'd think.  Sure, the stories can be mildly spooky, but they just aren't scary (and the punchline to the loli's was actually quite funny).  They are, however, quite engaging and interesting.  The style used to tell the stories was quite well done.
There is, however, an issue with typos and some grammatical errors that you'll notice upon reading this work.  Please keep in mind that it's completely developed by Russians and they did their best with the English translation.  (Can't blame them for that too much.  Of course,
was also developed by a Russian)
The characters, for the most part, didn't interest me...well, save for a few that is.  Sadly, half of their personalities just aren't there and most of their names are forgettable, much like in
(yes, that game has basically become a bar for comparison for me by now).  The portrait work takes a while to get used to, but by the end is quite nice.  The CG pictures and the background images are also quite well done.   As for the music?  Adrian von Ziegler's work(s) manage to make an appearance here, much like from
.  There's also multiple cues of the Metal Gear alert sound effect.  ("!")
Now, I'm kinda' a notorious slow reader, so I ended up clocking in 100 minutes from start to finish with breaks and moments where I needed to re-read some parts.  People have managed to skip most of this to get a final time of 0.1 hours, but I feel that many will finish reading it legit in less than 100 minutes.  An easy and relatively quick 100% for your list.

Awkward Dimensions Redux is a pretentious, edgy, art project. That said, all of those things make the experience quite memorable. The game plays very similar to "the beginners guide" in that you are going through different areas of someones creation and imprinting your own idea of what they mean. In the hour you spend with it, you will remember fond memories from your life, relax to some great music, view some nice art, climb a ladder (wew thats a tall ladder), and even feel emotional pain (depending on your mental state while playing).
Its strength lies in its ability to assume the player is introspective enough to carry forward with the task needed, and to have a sense of exploration. Its main weakness is that some of the visuals are harsh, as are some of the sound effects. These do not detract much from the game and in a sense contribute to the surreal nature of the dreamscapes you navigate.
Overall, it's a free game and if you've got an hour to kill where you want something relaxing to do, I highly suggest you give AWKWARD DIMENSIONS REDUX a shot.

A story about my uncle. I have no words after beating this game. A story about my uncle is an adventure game where you go through caves, villages and monsters to do nothing but look for your hipster gay uncle who's been smoking. (Check my screenshots if you want further proof). If you have anger management, or a hard time controlling your temper, this game is not for you as there are many situations after knowing exactly what you have to do that you will get ♥♥♥♥ed by some dumb pixel of ice that will make you slip off, which will "evaporate" all your hard work to get there. I have personally raged allot while playing this game, but the rage isn't going to change my mind about it being a GREAT game. The anger I had while playing this game was simply motivation to continue and to accomplish whatever I was having trouble with. Cons:
